**Shane Carruth** (born 1972) is an American filmmaker, known for science-fiction features in which he has filled numerous jobs, including [producer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_producer "Film producer"), [director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_director "Film director"), [screenwriter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screenwriter "Screenwriter"), [composer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Composer "Composer"), and [actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_actor "Film actor").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-about-com-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-2) These include his prize-winning debut [_Primer_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film) "Primer (film)") (2004) and _[Upstream Color](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upstream\_Color "Upstream Color")_ (2013). In reference to Carruth's unusual filmmaking technique, director [Steven Soderbergh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Soderbergh "Steven Soderbergh") described him as "the illegitimate offspring of [David Lynch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Lynch "David Lynch") and [James Cameron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Cameron "James Cameron")."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-EW-3)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shane_Carruth&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Carruth was born in [Myrtle Beach, South Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myrtle_Beach,_South_Carolina "Myrtle Beach, South Carolina") in 1972. He attended [Stephen F. Austin State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_F._Austin_State_University "Stephen F. Austin State University") as a mathematics major.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-4) Before becoming a filmmaker, he worked as a developer of [flight-simulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flight_simulator "Flight simulator") software.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-EW-3)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shane_Carruth&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### _Primer_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shane_Carruth&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Primer")]

Main article: [Primer (film)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film) "Primer (film)")

For his [independent film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_film "Independent film")_[Primer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer\_(film) "Primer (film)")_, Carruth wrote, directed, produced, and performed one of the two main roles; he also composed the [score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_score "Film score"). The film was honored at the 2004 [Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sundance_Film_Festival "Sundance Film Festival") with the Grand Jury Prize and the [Alfred P. Sloan Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_P._Sloan_Award "Alfred P. Sloan Award"). Carruth, a former software engineer with an undergraduate degree in mathematics,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-EW-3) used his technical knowledge extensively on the project.

### _Upstream Color_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shane_Carruth&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Upstream Color")]

Main article: [Upstream Color](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upstream_Color "Upstream Color")

On January 21, 2013, Carruth premiered his film _[Upstream Color](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upstream\_Color "Upstream Color")_ at the [2013 Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Sundance_Film_Festival "2013 Sundance Film Festival") in the U.S. Dramatic Competition category.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-5) Carruth, Johnny Marshall, and Pete Horner won the U.S. Dramatic Special Jury Award for Sound Design for the film.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-2013winners-6) Keith Kimbell wrote that it was the "most anticipated (and most difficult to describe) film in competition", and "most critics couldn't stop talking about it".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-kimbell-7) The film was released via [VHX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VHX "VHX") on April 5, 2013.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-kimbell-7) Some of Carruth's music from _Upstream Color_ was featured in the 2016 documentary _[Tickled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tickled "Tickled")_.

### Unrealized work

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shane_Carruth&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Unrealized work")]

In 2009, [David Sullivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Sullivan_(actor) "David Sullivan (actor)"), one of the leads in _Primer_, [tweeted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter") that "Shane Carruth's next project, _A Topiary_, is in the early stages of pre-production".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-8) Filmmaker [Rian Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rian_Johnson "Rian Johnson") tweeted that it would feature a "mind-blowing sci-fi script."[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-rcjohnso-tweet-9) In 2010, several news sources reported that _A Topiary_ was in the works and that the script had been written. There was already a website for the movie[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-10) which, according to Carruth in an interview to [io9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Io9 "Io9"), "The website for now is just a place mark as financing has yet to be completed. I'm cautiously optimistic that this can happen soon and couldn't be happier with the filmmakers that have committed to the project so far."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-11) However, the film (which _Entertainment Weekly_ described as "a sci-fi epic about a group of kids who build a giant, animal-like creature") stalled, and in early 2013, Carruth told _EW_ that it was "the thing I basically wasted my whole life on."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-EW-3) Carruth no longer pursues the project; some VFX test footage of the film is visible in _Upstream Color_ in a scene when a character is examining the video for technical flaws.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-12)

In 2014, Carruth announced a new film, _The Modern Ocean,_ based on [international shipping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship_transport "Ship transport") and the lives of those involved.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-13) On August 12, 2015, it was reported that the film was in pre-production,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-14) and its ensemble cast was announced in November 2015; it would include [Jeff Goldblum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Goldblum "Jeff Goldblum"), [Anne Hathaway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anne_Hathaway "Anne Hathaway"), [Keanu Reeves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keanu_Reeves "Keanu Reeves"), [Tom Holland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Holland "Tom Holland"), [Daniel Radcliffe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Radcliffe "Daniel Radcliffe"), [Chloë Grace Moretz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chlo%C3%AB_Grace_Moretz "Chloë Grace Moretz"), [Asa Butterfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asa_Butterfield "Asa Butterfield"), and [Abraham Attah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Attah "Abraham Attah").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-15) In an interview in 2018, Carruth noted that the film is "not gonna happen anytime soon".[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-16)[Irrfan Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irrfan_Khan "Irrfan Khan") was also scheduled to star as the lead captain of the ship, before his death on April 29, 2020. On June 17, 2020, Carruth posted the entire script for _The Modern Ocean_ on Twitter, along with some of the original score.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-18)

In 2019, in an interview Carruth claimed he was working on "a massive thing" and would leave the film industry once that project concludes.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-20)

### Consulting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shane_Carruth&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Consulting")]

Carruth was rumored to have consulted on [time-travel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_travel "Time travel") sequences for filmmaker [Rian Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rian_Johnson "Rian Johnson")'s [_Looper_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Looper_(film) "Looper (film)"), though it was later revealed that those sequences were deemed too expensive to shoot.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-22)

### Acting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shane_Carruth&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Acting")]

In 2018, Carruth starred in the psychological thriller _[The Dead Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Dead\_Center "The Dead Center")_ about a hospital psychiatrist whose own sanity is pushed to the edge when a frightened amnesiac patient insists that he has died and brought something terrible back from the other side.

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shane_Carruth&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Personal life")]

In 2019, when asked about his religious beliefs, he stated that he was raised Christian, but fell away from it, before later saying that he still prays from time to time and finds some comfort from the Bible.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-23)

### Legal issues

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shane_Carruth&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Legal issues")]

From 2011 to 2018, Carruth was in a relationship with [Amy Seimetz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amy_Seimetz "Amy Seimetz"). The couple became engaged in 2013.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-26) Seimetz obtained temporary restraining orders against Carruth in 2018 and a permanent restraining order in 2020, citing years of domestic and emotional abuse and harassment.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-28) Carruth has denied these allegations.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-29)

On January 13, 2022, Carruth was arrested at the home of another ex-girlfriend on allegations of domestic assault and vandalism. He was released four days later on a $50,000 bond. _[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety\_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)")_ reported that the Los Angeles County District Attorney's Office would not file felony charges.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-30)

**Shane Carruth** (born 1972) is an American filmmaker, known for science-fiction features in which he has filled numerous jobs, including [producer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_producer "Film producer"), [director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_director "Film director"), [screenwriter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screenwriter "Screenwriter"), [composer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Composer "Composer"), and [actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_actor "Film actor").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-about-com-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-2) These include his prize-winning debut [_Primer_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film) "Primer (film)") (2004) and _[Upstream Color](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upstream\_Color "Upstream Color")_ (2013). In reference to Carruth's unusual filmmaking technique, director [Steven Soderbergh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Soderbergh "Steven Soderbergh") described him as "the illegitimate offspring of [David Lynch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Lynch "David Lynch") and [James Cameron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Cameron "James Cameron")."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-EW-3)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shane_Carruth&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Carruth was born in [Myrtle Beach, South Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myrtle_Beach,_South_Carolina "Myrtle Beach, South Carolina") in 1972. He attended [Stephen F. Austin State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_F._Austin_State_University "Stephen F. Austin State University") as a mathematics major.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-4) Before becoming a filmmaker, he worked as a developer of [flight-simulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flight_simulator "Flight simulator") software.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-EW-3)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shane_Carruth&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### _Primer_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shane_Carruth&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Primer")]

Main article: [Primer (film)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film) "Primer (film)")

For his [independent film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_film "Independent film")_[Primer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer\_(film) "Primer (film)")_, Carruth wrote, directed, produced, and performed one of the two main roles; he also composed the [score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_score "Film score"). The film was honored at the 2004 [Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sundance_Film_Festival "Sundance Film Festival") with the Grand Jury Prize and the [Alfred P. Sloan Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_P._Sloan_Award "Alfred P. Sloan Award"). Carruth, a former software engineer with an undergraduate degree in mathematics,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-EW-3) used his technical knowledge extensively on the project.

### _Upstream Color_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shane_Carruth&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Upstream Color")]

Main article: [Upstream Color](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upstream_Color "Upstream Color")

On January 21, 2013, Carruth premiered his film _[Upstream Color](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upstream\_Color "Upstream Color")_ at the [2013 Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Sundance_Film_Festival "2013 Sundance Film Festival") in the U.S. Dramatic Competition category.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-5) Carruth, Johnny Marshall, and Pete Horner won the U.S. Dramatic Special Jury Award for Sound Design for the film.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-2013winners-6) Keith Kimbell wrote that it was the "most anticipated (and most difficult to describe) film in competition", and "most critics couldn't stop talking about it".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-kimbell-7) The film was released via [VHX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VHX "VHX") on April 5, 2013.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-kimbell-7) Some of Carruth's music from _Upstream Color_ was featured in the 2016 documentary _[Tickled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tickled "Tickled")_.

### Unrealized work

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shane_Carruth&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Unrealized work")]

In 2009, [David Sullivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Sullivan_(actor) "David Sullivan (actor)"), one of the leads in _Primer_, [tweeted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter") that "Shane Carruth's next project, _A Topiary_, is in the early stages of pre-production".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-8) Filmmaker [Rian Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rian_Johnson "Rian Johnson") tweeted that it would feature a "mind-blowing sci-fi script."[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-rcjohnso-tweet-9) In 2010, several news sources reported that _A Topiary_ was in the works and that the script had been written. There was already a website for the movie[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-10) which, according to Carruth in an interview to [io9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Io9 "Io9"), "The website for now is just a place mark as financing has yet to be completed. I'm cautiously optimistic that this can happen soon and couldn't be happier with the filmmakers that have committed to the project so far."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-11) However, the film (which _Entertainment Weekly_ described as "a sci-fi epic about a group of kids who build a giant, animal-like creature") stalled, and in early 2013, Carruth told _EW_ that it was "the thing I basically wasted my whole life on."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-EW-3) Carruth no longer pursues the project; some VFX test footage of the film is visible in _Upstream Color_ in a scene when a character is examining the video for technical flaws.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-12)

In 2014, Carruth announced a new film, _The Modern Ocean,_ based on [international shipping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship_transport "Ship transport") and the lives of those involved.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-13) On August 12, 2015, it was reported that the film was in pre-production,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-14) and its ensemble cast was announced in November 2015; it would include [Jeff Goldblum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Goldblum "Jeff Goldblum"), [Anne Hathaway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anne_Hathaway "Anne Hathaway"), [Keanu Reeves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keanu_Reeves "Keanu Reeves"), [Tom Holland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Holland "Tom Holland"), [Daniel Radcliffe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Radcliffe "Daniel Radcliffe"), [Chloë Grace Moretz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chlo%C3%AB_Grace_Moretz "Chloë Grace Moretz"), [Asa Butterfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asa_Butterfield "Asa Butterfield"), and [Abraham Attah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Attah "Abraham Attah").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-15) In an interview in 2018, Carruth noted that the film is "not gonna happen anytime soon".[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-16)[Irrfan Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irrfan_Khan "Irrfan Khan") was also scheduled to star as the lead captain of the ship, before his death on April 29, 2020. On June 17, 2020, Carruth posted the entire script for _The Modern Ocean_ on Twitter, along with some of the original score.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-18)

In 2019, in an interview Carruth claimed he was working on "a massive thing" and would leave the film industry once that project concludes.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-20)

### Consulting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shane_Carruth&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Consulting")]

Carruth was rumored to have consulted on [time-travel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_travel "Time travel") sequences for filmmaker [Rian Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rian_Johnson "Rian Johnson")'s [_Looper_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Looper_(film) "Looper (film)"), though it was later revealed that those sequences were deemed too expensive to shoot.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-22)

### Acting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shane_Carruth&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Acting")]

In 2018, Carruth starred in the psychological thriller _[The Dead Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Dead\_Center "The Dead Center")_ about a hospital psychiatrist whose own sanity is pushed to the edge when a frightened amnesiac patient insists that he has died and brought something terrible back from the other side.

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shane_Carruth&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Personal life")]

In 2019, when asked about his religious beliefs, he stated that he was raised Christian, but fell away from it, before later saying that he still prays from time to time and finds some comfort from the Bible.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-23)

### Legal issues

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shane_Carruth&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Legal issues")]

From 2011 to 2018, Carruth was in a relationship with [Amy Seimetz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amy_Seimetz "Amy Seimetz"). The couple became engaged in 2013.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-26) Seimetz obtained temporary restraining orders against Carruth in 2018 and a permanent restraining order in 2020, citing years of domestic and emotional abuse and harassment.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-28) Carruth has denied these allegations.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-29)

On January 13, 2022, Carruth was arrested at the home of another ex-girlfriend on allegations of domestic assault and vandalism. He was released four days later on a $50,000 bond. _[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety\_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)")_ reported that the Los Angeles County District Attorney's Office would not file felony charges.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Carruth#cite_note-30)

A **sibling** is a relative that shares at least one [parent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parent "Parent") with the other person. A [male](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Male "Male") sibling is a [brother](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brother "Brother"), and a [female](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Female "Female") sibling is a [sister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sister "Sister"). A person with no siblings is an [only child](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Only_child "Only child").

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/16/Me_and_my_other_brother.jpg/250px-Me_and_my_other_brother.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Me_and_my_other_brother.jpg)

A [sister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sister "Sister") (female sibling) carrying her [brother](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brother "Brother") (male sibling).

While some circumstances can cause siblings to be raised separately (such as [foster care](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foster_care "Foster care") or [adoption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adoption "Adoption")), most societies have siblings grow up together. This causes the development of strong [emotional bonds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_bonding "Human bonding"), with siblinghood considered a unique type of relationship. The emotional bond between siblings is often complicated and is influenced by factors such as parental treatment, [birth order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_order "Birth order"), [personality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personality_psychology "Personality psychology"), and personal experiences outside the family.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-psychtoday-1)

Medically, a full-sibling is a [first-degree relative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First-degree_relative "First-degree relative") and a half-sibling is a [second-degree relative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second-degree_relative "Second-degree relative") as they are related by 50% and 25%, respectively.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-3)

## Definitions

The word _sibling_ was reintroduced in 1903 in an article in _[Biometrika](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biometrika "Biometrika")_, as a translation for the German _Geschwister_, having not been used since Middle English, specifically 1425.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-5)

Siblings or **full-siblings** ([_full_] _sisters_ or _brothers_) share the same biological parents. Full-siblings are also the most common type of siblings.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-6)[Twins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twin "Twin") are siblings that are born from the same [pregnancy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pregnancy "Pregnancy").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-7) Twins generally share a greater bond due to growing up together and being the same age.

**Half-siblings** (**half-sisters** or **half-brothers**) are people who share one parent. They may share the same mother but different fathers (in which case they are known as _uterine_ siblings or _maternal half-siblings_), or they may have the same father but different mothers (in which case, they are known as _agnate_ siblings or _paternal half-siblings_. In law, the term _[consanguine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consanguinity "Consanguinity")_ is used in place of [agnate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agnate "Agnate")).[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] In law (and especially [inheritance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inheritance "Inheritance") law), half-siblings have often been accorded treatment unequal to that of full-siblings. Old English [common law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_law "Common law") at one time incorporated inequalities into the laws of [intestate succession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intestacy "Intestacy"), with half-siblings taking only half as much property of their [intestate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intestacy "Intestacy") siblings' estates as siblings of full-blood. Unequal treatment of this type has been wholly abolished in [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England "England"),[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-8) but still exists in Florida.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-9)

**Three-quarter siblings** share one parent, while the unshared parents are [first-degree relatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First-degree_relatives "First-degree relatives") to each other, for example, if a man has children with two women who are sisters, or a woman has children with a man and his son. In the first case, the children are half-siblings as well as first cousins; in the second, the children are half-siblings as well as a half-avuncular pair. They are genetically closer than half-siblings but less genetically close than full-siblings,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-10) a degree of genetic relationship that is rare in humans and little-studied.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-11) One notable example of three-quarter siblings is the family of American aviator [Charles Lindbergh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Lindbergh "Charles Lindbergh"), who fathered children with two German sisters, Brigitte and Marietta Hesshaimer.

[Diblings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dibling "Dibling"), a portmanteau of donor sibling, or donor-conceived sibling, or donor-sperm sibling, are biologically connected through [donated eggs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egg_donation "Egg donation") or [sperm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sperm_donation "Sperm donation").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-guardian-jolly-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-13) Diblings are biologically siblings though not legally for the purposes of family rights and inheritance. The anonymity of donation is seen to add complication to the process of courtship.

### Non-blood relations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sibling&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Non-blood relations")]

Related through affinity:

*   **[Stepsiblings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stepsibling "Stepsibling")** (stepbrothers or stepsisters) are the children of one's [stepparent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stepfamily "Stepfamily") from a previous relationship.
*   **Adoptive siblings** are raised by a person who is the [adoptive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adoption "Adoption") parent of one and the adoptive or biological parent of the other.
*   **[Siblings-in-law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sibling-in-law "Sibling-in-law")** are the siblings of one's spouse, the spouse of one's sibling, or the spouse of one's spouse's sibling.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-15) The spouse of one's spouse's sibling may also be called a **co-sibling**.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-17)

Not related:

*   **Foster siblings** are children who are raised in the same [foster home](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foster_home "Foster home"): foster children of one's parent(s), or the children or foster children of one's foster parent.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-20)
*   **God siblings** are the children of the [godfather or godmother](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Godparent "Godparent") or the godchildren of the father or mother.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
*   **Milk siblings** are children who have been [nursed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breastfeeding "Breastfeeding") by the same woman. This relationship exists in cultures with [milk kinship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milk_kinship "Milk kinship") and in [Islamic law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_law "Islamic law").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-21)
*   **Cross-siblings** are individuals who share one or more half-siblings; if one person has at least one maternal half-sibling and at least one paternal half-sibling, the maternal and paternal half-siblings are cross-siblings to each other.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-22)[_[dubious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Accuracy\_dispute#Disputed\_statement "Wikipedia:Accuracy dispute")–[discuss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:Sibling#Cross\_siblings? "Talk:Sibling")_]

## Consanguinity and genetics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sibling&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Consanguinity and genetics")]

[Consanguinity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consanguinity "Consanguinity") is the measure of how closely people are related.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-23) Genetic relatedness measures how many genes a person shares. As all humans share over 99% of the same genes, consanguinity only matters for the small fraction of genes which vary between different people.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-Ask_a_Geneticist_2006-24) Inheritance of genes has a random element to it,[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-Ask_a_Geneticist_2006-24) and these two concepts are different.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-Ask_a_Geneticist_2013-25) Consanguinity decreases by half for every generation of reproductive separation through their most recent common ancestor. Siblings are 50% related by consanguinity as they are separated from each other by two generation (sibling to parent to sibling), and they share two parents as common ancestors ({\displaystyle \left({\tfrac {1}{2}}\right)^{2}+\left({\tfrac {1}{2}}\right)^{2}}![Image 8: {\displaystyle \left({\tfrac {1}{2}}\right)^{2}+\left({\tfrac {1}{2}}\right)^{2}}](https://wikimedia.org/api/rest_v1/media/math/render/svg/498a35be41ff49ab5ae747550a8b9a3075022add)).

A fraternal twin is a sibling and, therefore, is related by 50% consanguinity.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-26)[Fraternal twins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraternal_twins "Fraternal twins") are no more genetically similar than regular siblings. As [identical twins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Identical_twin "Identical twin") come from the same zygote, their most recent common ancestor is each other. They’re genetically identical and 100% consanguineous as they’re separated by zero generations ({\displaystyle \left({\tfrac {1}{2}}\right)^{0}}![Image 9: {\displaystyle \left({\tfrac {1}{2}}\right)^{0}}](https://wikimedia.org/api/rest_v1/media/math/render/svg/f267aa6421f2c8408f11bfadc817523fbce7e955)).[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-Ask_a_Geneticist_2006-24)[Twin studies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twin_study "Twin study") have been conducted by scientists to examine the roles that [genetics and environment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nature_versus_nurture "Nature versus nurture") play in the development of various traits. Such studies examine how often identical twins possess the same behavioral trait and compare it to how often fraternal twins possess the same trait.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-27) In other studies twins are raised in separate families, and studies compare the passing on of a behavioral trait by the family environment and the possession of a common trait between identical twins. This kind of study has revealed that for personality traits which are known to be [heritable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heritability "Heritability"), genetics play a substantial role throughout life and an even larger role during early years.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-28)

Half-siblings are 25% related by consanguinity as they share one parent and separated from each other by two generations ({\displaystyle \left({\tfrac {1}{2}}\right)^{2}}![Image 10: {\displaystyle \left({\tfrac {1}{2}}\right)^{2}}](https://wikimedia.org/api/rest_v1/media/math/render/svg/331f0b46005d99ab124f6e6d8b4a8f19982cc5ee)).

A person may share more than the standard consanguinity with their sibling if their parents are closely biologically related (the [coefficient of inbreeding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coefficient_of_inbreeding "Coefficient of inbreeding") is greater than zero).[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]Interestingly, half-siblings can be related by as "three-quarters siblings" (related by 3/8) if their unshared parents have a consanguinity of 50%. This means the unshared parents are either siblings, making the half-siblings [cousins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cousin "Cousin"), or parent and child, making them half- [aunt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aunt "Aunt")-[uncle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncle "Uncle") and [niece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niece "Niece")-[nephew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nephew "Nephew").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-29)

### Percentage distribution

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sibling&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Percentage distribution")]

In practice, full siblings do not share exactly 50% of their DNA, as [chromosomal crossover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosomal_crossover "Chromosomal crossover") only occurs a limited number of times and, therefore, large chunks of a chromosome are shared or not shared at one time. In fact, the mean DNA fraction shared is 50.28% with a standard deviation of 3.68%,[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-30) meaning approximately 1/4 of sibling pairs share more than 52.76% of their DNA, while 1/4 share less than 47.8%.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-31)

There is a very small chance that two half-siblings might not share any genes if they didn't inherit any of the same chromosomes from their shared parent. This is possible for full-siblings as well, though even more unlikely. But because of how [homologous chromosomes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homologous_chromosomes "Homologous chromosomes") swap genes (due to [chromosomal crossover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosomal_crossover "Chromosomal crossover") during [meiosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meiosis "Meiosis")) during the development of an egg or sperm cell, however, the odds of this ever actually occurring are practically non-existent.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-Ask_a_Geneticist_2013-25)

Birth order is a person's rank by age among their siblings. Typically, researchers classify siblings as "eldest", "middle child", and "youngest" or simply distinguish between "first-born" and "later-born" children.

Birth order is commonly believed in [pop psychology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_psychology "Pop psychology") and popular culture to have a profound and lasting effect on psychological development and [personality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personality_psychology "Personality psychology"). For example, firstborns are seen as conservative and high-achieving, middle children as natural mediators, and youngest children as charming and outgoing. Despite its lasting presence in the public domain, studies have failed to consistently produce clear, valid, compelling findings; therefore, it has earned the title of a [pseudo-psychology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pseudoscience "Pseudoscience") amongst the scientific psychological community.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-Psychology_Around_Us-32)

### History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sibling&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: History")]

The theorizing and study of birth order can be traced back to [Francis Galton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_Galton "Francis Galton")'s (1822–1911) theory of birth order and [eminence](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/eminence "wikt:eminence") and [Alfred Adler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Adler "Alfred Adler")'s (1870–1937) theory of birth order and personality characteristics.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-35)

#### Galton

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sibling&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Galton")]

In his book _English Men of Science: Their Nature and Nurture_ (1874), Galton noted that prominent composers and scientists are over-represented as first-borns.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-intelltheory.com-36) He theorized three main reasons as to why first-borns are generally more eminent:

1.   [Primogeniture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primogeniture "Primogeniture") laws: first-borns have access to their parents' financial resources to continue their education.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-intelltheory.com-36)
2.   First-borns are given more responsibility than their younger siblings and are treated more as companions by their parents.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-intelltheory.com-36)
3.   First-borns are given more attention and nourishment in families with limited financial resources.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-intelltheory.com-36)

#### Adler

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sibling&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Adler")]

*   First Borns: Fulfilling family roles of leadership and authority, obedient of protocol and hierarchy. Seek out and prefer order, structure and adherence to norms and rules. They partake in goal-striving behaviour as their lives are centred around achievement and accomplishment themes. They fear the loss of their position in the top of the hierarchy.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceA-37)
*   Middle Children: Feel like outcasts of families as they lack primacy of the first child and the "attention garnering recency" of the youngest. These children often go to great lengths to de-identify themselves with their siblings, in an attempt to make a different and individualized identity for themselves as they feel like they were "squeezed out" of their families.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceA-37)
*   Youngest Children: Feel disadvantaged compared to older siblings, are often perceived as less capable or experienced and are therefore indulged and spoiled. Because of this, they are skilled in coaxing/charming others to do things for them or provide. This contributes to the image of them being popular and outgoing, as they engage in attention-seeking behaviour to meet their needs.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-38)

### Contemporary findings

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sibling&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Contemporary findings")]

The flaws and inconsistencies in birth order research eliminate its validity. It is very difficult to control solely for factors related to birth order, and therefore most studies produce ambiguous results.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceA-37) Embedded into theories of birth order is a debate of nature versus nurture. It has been disproved that there is something innate in the position one is born into, and therefore creating a preset role. Birth order has no genetic basis.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-39)

The social interaction that occurs as a result of birth order however is the most notable. Older siblings often become role models of behaviour, and younger siblings become learners and supervisees. Older siblings are at a developmental advantage both cognitively and socially. The role of birth order also depends greatly and varies greatly on family context. Family size, sibling identification, age gap, modeling, parenting techniques, gender, class, race, and temperament are all confounding variables that can influence behaviour and therefore perceived behaviour of specific birth categories.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-40) The research on birth order does have stronger correlations, however, in areas such as intelligence and physical features, but are likely caused by other factors other than the actual position of birth. Some research has found that firstborn children have slightly higher [IQs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IQ "IQ") on average than later born children.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-41) However, other research finds no such effect.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-42) It has been found that first-borns score three points higher compared to second borns and that children born earlier in a family are on average, taller and weigh more than those born later.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-Psychology_Around_Us-32) However, it is impossible to generalize birth order characteristics and apply them universally to all individuals in that subgroup.

#### Contemporary explanations for IQ findings

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sibling&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Contemporary explanations for IQ findings")]

##### Resource dilution model

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sibling&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Resource dilution model")]

(Blake, 1981) provide three potential reasons for the higher scoring of older siblings on IQ tests:[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-intelltheory.com-36)

1.   Parental resources are finite, first-born children get full and primary access to these resources.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-intelltheory.com-36)
2.   As the number of a children in a family goes up, the more resources must be shared.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-intelltheory.com-36)
3.   These parental resources have an important impact on a child's educational success.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-intelltheory.com-36)

##### Confluence model

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sibling&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Confluence model")]

[Robert Zajonc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Zajonc "Robert Zajonc") proposed that the intellectual environment within a family is ever-changing due to three factors, and therefore more permissive of first-born children's intellectual advancement:[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-intelltheory.com-36)

1.   Firstborns do not need to share parental attention and have their parents' complete absorption. More siblings in the family limit the attention devoted to each of them.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-intelltheory.com-36)
2.   Firstborns are exposed to more adult language. Later-borns are exposed to the less-mature speech of their older siblings.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-intelltheory.com-36)
3.   Firstborns and older siblings must answer questions and explain things to younger siblings, acting as tutors. This advances their cognitive processing of information and language skills.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-intelltheory.com-36)

In 1996, interest in the science behind birth order was re-sparked when [Frank Sulloway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Sulloway "Frank Sulloway")’s book _Born To Rebel_ was published. In this book, Sulloway argues that firstborns are more conscientious, more socially dominant, less agreeable, and less open to new ideas compared to later-borns. While being seemingly empirical and academic, as many studies are cited throughout the book, it is still often criticized as a biased and incomplete account of the whole picture of siblings and birth order. Because it is a novel, the research and theories proposed throughout were not criticized and peer-reviewed by other academics before its release.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-43)[Literature reviews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Literature_review "Literature review") that have examined many studies and attempted to control for confounding variables tend to find minimal effects for birth order on personality.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-45) In her review of the scientific literature, [Judith Rich Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judith_Rich_Harris "Judith Rich Harris") suggests that birth order effects may exist within the context of the family of origin, but that they are not enduring aspects of personality.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-46)

In practice, systematic birth order research is a challenge because it is difficult to control for all of the variables that are statistically related to birth order. For example, large families are generally lower in socioeconomic status than small families, so third-born children are more likely than first-born children to come from poorer families. Spacing of children, parenting style, and gender are additional variables to consider.

Regressive behaviors are the child's way of demanding the parents' love and attention.

The arrival of a new baby is especially stressful for firstborns and for siblings between 3 and 5 years old. In such situations, regressive behavior may be accompanied by aggressive behavior, such as handling the baby roughly. All of these symptoms are considered to be typical and developmentally appropriate for children between the ages of 3 and 5. While some can be prevented, the remainder can be improved within a few months. Regressive behavior may include demand for a bottle, [thumb sucking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thumb_sucking "Thumb sucking"), requests to wear diapers (even if toilet-trained), or requests to carry a [security blanket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Security_blanket "Security blanket").

The [American Academy of Pediatrics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Academy_of_Pediatrics "American Academy of Pediatrics") suggests that instead of protesting or telling children to act their age, parents should simply grant their requests without becoming upset. The affected children will soon return to their normal routine when they realize that they now have just as important a place in the family as the new sibling. Most of the behaviors can be improved within a few months.

The [University of Michigan Health System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Michigan_Health_System "University of Michigan Health System") advises that most occurrences of regressive behavior are mild and to be expected; however, it recommends parents to contact a pediatrician or child psychologist if the older child tries to hurt the baby, if regressive behavior does not improve within 2 or 3 months, or if the parents have other questions or concerns.

## Rivalry

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sibling&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Rivalry")]

Main article: [Sibling rivalry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sibling_rivalry "Sibling rivalry")

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/14/Sir_Joshua_Reynolds_-_Lady_Cockburn_and_Her_Three_Eldest_Sons_%281773-1775%29.jpg/250px-Sir_Joshua_Reynolds_-_Lady_Cockburn_and_Her_Three_Eldest_Sons_%281773-1775%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sir_Joshua_Reynolds_-_Lady_Cockburn_and_Her_Three_Eldest_Sons_(1773-1775).jpg)

_[Portrait of Lady Cockburn and her Three Eldest Sons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portrait\_of\_Lady\_Cockburn\_and\_her\_Three\_Eldest\_Sons "Portrait of Lady Cockburn and her Three Eldest Sons")_ (1773–1775) by [Joshua Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joshua_Reynolds "Joshua Reynolds")

"Sibling rivalry" is a type of competition or animosity among brothers and sisters. It appears to be particularly intense when children are very close in age or of the same gender.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-47) Sibling rivalry can involve [aggression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aggression "Aggression"); however, it is not the same as [sibling abuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sibling_abuse "Sibling abuse") where one child victimizes another.

Sibling rivalry usually starts right after, or before, the arrival of the second child. While siblings will still love each other, it is not uncommon for them to bicker and be malicious to each other.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-newbaby-48) Children are sensitive from the age of 1 year to differences in parental treatment and by 3 years they have a sophisticated grasp of family rules and can evaluate themselves in relation to their siblings.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-psychtoday-1) Sibling rivalry often continues throughout childhood and can be very frustrating and stressful to parents.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-michigan-49) One study found that the age group 10–15 reported the highest level of competition between siblings.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-mcnerney-50) This competition can also cause [behavioral spillover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behavioral_spillover "Behavioral spillover") where siblings, intentionally or not, influence each other's life trajectories in a positive manner as they attempt to differentiate and challenge themselves to excel, vying for their parents' praise.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-nytimes-51)

Sibling rivalry can continue into adulthood and sibling relationships can change dramatically over the years. Approximately one-third of adults describe their relationship with siblings as rivalrous or distant. However, rivalry often lessens over time and at least 80% of siblings over age 60 enjoy close ties.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-psychtoday-1)

Each child in a family competes to define who they are as persons and want to show that they are separate from their siblings. Sibling rivalry increases when children feel they are getting unequal amounts of their parents' attention, where there is stress in the parents' and children's lives, and where fighting is accepted by the family as a way to resolve conflicts.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-michigan-49)[Sigmund Freud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sigmund_Freud "Sigmund Freud") saw the sibling relationship as an extension of the [Oedipus complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oedipus_complex "Oedipus complex"), where brothers were in competition for their mother's attention and sisters for their father's.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-52)[Evolutionary psychologists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_psychologist "Evolutionary psychologist") explain sibling rivalry in terms of [parental investment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parental_investment "Parental investment") and [kin selection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kin_selection "Kin selection"): a parent is inclined to spread resources equally among all children in the family, but a child wants most of the resources for him or herself.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-mcnerney-50)

## Relationships

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sibling&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Relationships")]

Further information: [Sibling relationship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sibling_relationship "Sibling relationship")

### Jealousy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sibling&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Jealousy")]

See also: [Attachment theory § Attachment patterns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attachment_theory#Attachment_patterns "Attachment theory")

[Jealousy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jealousy "Jealousy") is not a single emotion. The basic emotions expressed in jealous interactions are [fear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fear "Fear"), [anger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anger "Anger"), relief, [sadness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sadness "Sadness"), and anxiety.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceB-53) Jealousy occurs in a social triangle of relationships which do not require a third person. The social triangle involves the relationships between the jealous individual and the parent, the relationship between the parent and the rival, and the relationship between jealous individual and the rival.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceB-53)

#### Newborn

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sibling&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Newborn")]

First-borns' attachment to their parents is directly related to their jealous behaviour. In a study by Volling, four classes of children were identified based on their different responses of jealousy to new infant siblings and parent interactions.

*   **Regulated Exploration Children**: 60% of children fall into this category.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceB-53) These children closely watch their parents interact with their newborn sibling, approach them positively and sometimes join the interaction.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceB-53) They show fewer behaviour problems in the months following the new birth and do not display problematic behaviours during the parent-infant interaction.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceB-53) These children are considered [secure](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/secure "wikt:secure") as they act how a child would be expected to act in a familiar home setting with their parents present as secure bases to explore the environment.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceB-53)
*   **Approach-Avoidant Children**: 30% of children fall into this category.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceB-53) These children observe parent-infant interaction closely and are less likely to approach the infant and the parent. They are anxious to explore the new environment as they tend to seek little comfort from their parents.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceB-53)
*   **[Anxious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anxious "Anxious")-Clingy Children**: 6% of children fell into this category. These children have an intense interest in parent-infant interaction and a strong desire to seek proximity and contact with the parent, and sometimes intrude on parent-child interaction.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceB-53)
*   **Disruptive Children**: 2.7% of children fall into this category.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceB-53) These children are emotionally reactive and aggressive. They have difficulty regulating their negative emotions and may be likely to externalize it as negative behaviour around the newborn.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceB-53)

#### Parental effect

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sibling&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Parental effect")]

Children are more jealous of the interactions between newborns and their mothers than they are with newborns and their fathers.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceB-53) This is logical as up until the birth of the infant, the first-born child had the mother as their primary care-giver all to themselves. Some research has suggested that children display less jealous reactions over father-newborn interactions because fathers tend to punish negative [emotion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emotion "Emotion") and are less tolerant than mothers of clinginess and visible distress, although this is hard to generalize.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceB-53)

Children that have parents with a better marital relationship are better at regulating their jealous emotions.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceB-53) Children are more likely to express jealousy when their parents are directing their attention to the sibling as opposed to when the parents are solely interacting with them.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceB-53) Parents who are involved in good marital communication help their children cope adaptively with jealousy. They do this by modelling problem-solving and conflict resolution for their children. Children are also less likely to have jealous feelings when they live in a home in which everyone in the family shares and expresses love and happiness.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceB-53)

#### Implicit theories

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sibling&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Implicit theories")]

Implicit theories about relationships are associated with the ways children think of strategies to deal with a new situation. Children can fall into two categories of implicit theorizing. They may be malleable theorists and believe that they can affect change on situations and people. Alternatively, they may be fixed theorists, believing situations and people are not changeable.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceC-54) These implicit beliefs determine both the intensity of their jealous feelings, and how long those jealous feelings last.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceC-54)

*   **Malleable Theorists** display engaging behaviours, like interacting with the parent or sibling in an attempt to improve the situation.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceC-54) They tend to have more intense and longer-lasting feelings of jealousy because they spend more time ruminating on the situation and constructing ways to make it better.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceC-54)
*   **Fixed Theorists** display non-engaging behaviours, for example retreating to their room because they believe none of their actions will affect or improve the situation.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceC-54) They tend to have less intense and shorter lasting feelings of jealousy than malleable theorists.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceC-54)

#### Different ages

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sibling&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Different ages")]

Older children tend to be less jealous than their younger sibling.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceB-53) This is due to their ability to mentally process the social situation in a way that gives them more positive, empathetic feelings toward their younger sibling.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceB-53) Older children are better able to cope with their jealous feelings toward their younger sibling due to their understanding of the necessary relationship between the parent and younger sibling.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceB-53) Older children are also better at self-regulating their emotions and are less dependent on their caregivers for external regulation as opposed to their younger siblings.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceB-53) Younger siblings' feelings of jealousy are overpowered by feelings of anger.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceB-53) The quality of the relationship between the younger child and the older child is also a factor in jealousy, as the better the relationship the less jealous feelings occurred and vice versa.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceB-53)

### Conflict

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sibling&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Conflict")]

Sibling conflict is pervasive and often shrugged off as an accepted part of sibling dynamics. In spite of the broad variety of conflict that siblings are often involved in, sibling conflicts can be grouped into two broader categories.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceD-55) The first category is conflict about equality or fairness. It is not uncommon to see siblings who think that their sibling is favored by their teachers, peers, or especially their parents. In fact it is not uncommon to see siblings who both think that their parents favor the other sibling. Perceived inequalities in the division of resources such as who got a larger dessert also fall into this category of conflict. This form of conflict seems to be more prevalent in the younger sibling.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceD-55)

The second category of conflict involves an invasion of a child's perceived personal domain by their sibling. An example of this type of conflict is when a child enters their sibling's room when they are not welcome, or when a child crosses over into their sibling's side of the car in a long road trip. These types of fights seem to be more important to older siblings due to their larger desire for independence.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceD-55)

### Warmth

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sibling&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Warmth")]

Sibling warmth is a term for the degree of affection and companionship shared by siblings. Sibling warmth seems to have an effect on siblings. Higher sibling warmth is related to better [social skill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_skill "Social skill") and higher perceived social competence. Even in cases where there is a high level of sibling conflict if there is also a high level of sibling warmth then social skills and competence remain unaffected.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceE-56)

### Negative effects of conflict

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sibling&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Negative effects of conflict")]

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3b/Sibling_Conflict.jpg/250px-Sibling_Conflict.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sibling_Conflict.jpg)

Sibling physical conflict

The saying that people "fight like siblings" shows just how charged sibling conflict can be and how well recognized sibling squabbles are. In spite of how widely acknowledged these squabbles can be, sibling conflict can have several impacts on the sibling pair. It has been shown that increased levels of sibling conflict are related to higher levels of anxiety and depression in siblings, along with lower levels of self-worth and lower levels of academic competence. In addition, sibling warmth is not a protective factor for the negative effects of [anxiety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anxiety "Anxiety"), [depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depression_(mood) "Depression (mood)"), lack of [self-worth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-worth "Self-worth") and lower levels of academic competence. This means that sibling warmth does not counteract these negative effects.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceE-56) Sibling conflict is also linked to an increase in more risky behavior including: smoking cigarettes, skipping days of school, contact with the police, and other behaviors in Caucasian sibling pairs with the exception of firstborns with younger brothers. Except for the elder brother in this pair sibling conflict is positively correlated with risky behavior, thus sibling conflict may be a [risk factor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Risk_factor_(disambiguation) "Risk factor (disambiguation)") for behavioral problems.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-57) A study on what the topic of the fight was (invasion of personal domain or inequality) also shows that the topic of the fight may have a result on the effects of the conflict. This study showed that sibling conflict over personal domain were related to lower levels of self-esteem, and sibling conflict over perceived inequalities seem to be more related to depressive symptoms. However, the study also showed that greater depressive and anxious symptoms were also related to more frequent sibling conflict and more intense sibling conflict.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-ReferenceD-55)

### Parental management techniques of conflict

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sibling&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Parental management techniques of conflict")]

Techniques used by parents to manage their children's conflicts include parental non-intervention, child-centered parental intervention strategies, and more rarely the encouragement of physical conflict between siblings. Parental non-intervention included techniques in which the parent ignores the siblings' conflict and lets them work it out between themselves without outside guidance. In some cases, this technique is chosen to avoid situations in which the parent decides which sibling is in the right and may favor one sibling over the other, however, by following this technique the parent may sacrifice the opportunity to instruct their children on how to deal with conflict. Child-centered parental interventions include techniques in which the parent mediates the argument between the two children and helps them come to an agreement. Using this technique, parents may help model how the children can deal with conflicts in the future; however, parents should avoid dictating the outcome to the children, and make sure that they are mediating the argument making suggestions, allowing the children to decide the outcome. This may be especially important when some of the children have autism.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-58) Techniques in which parents encourage physical aggression between siblings may be chosen by the parents to help children deal with aggression in the future, however, this technique does not appear to be effective as it is linked to greater conflict levels between children. Parental non-intervention is also linked to higher levels of sibling conflict, and lower levels of sibling warmth. It appears that child-centered parental interventions have the best effect on sibling's relationship with a link to greater levels of sibling warmth and lower levels of sibling conflict.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-59)

### Long-term effects of presence

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sibling&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Long-term effects of presence")]

Studies on social skill and personality differences between [only children](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Only_child "Only child") and children with siblings suggest that overall the presence of a sibling does not have any effect on the child as an adult.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-60) However, working-class families who do not have the income for their children to participate in extracurricular activities such as sports or academia can benefit culturally and intellectually from the increased time those siblings spend together.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-nytimes-51)

## Gender roles among children and parents

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sibling&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: Gender roles among children and parents")]

There have always been some differences between siblings, especially different sex siblings. Often, different sex sibling may consider things to be unfair because their brother or sister is allowed to do certain things because of their gender, while they get to do something less fun or just different. McHale and her colleague conducted a [longitudinal study](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Longitudinal_study "Longitudinal study") using middle-childhood aged children and observed the way in which the parents contributed to stereotypical attitudes in their kids. In their study the experimenters analysed two different types of families, one with the same sex siblings, and the other with different sex siblings, as well as the children's birth order.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-McHale99-61) The experiment was conducted using phone interviews, in which the experimenters would ask the children about the activities they performed throughout their day outside of school.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-McHale99-61) The experimenters found that in the homes where there were mixed gender kids, and the father held traditional values, the kids also held traditional values and therefore also played gender based roles in the home.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-McHale99-61) In contrast, in homes where the father did not hold traditional values, the house chores were divided more equally among his kids.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-McHale99-61) However, if fathers had two male children, the younger male tended to help more with household chores, but as he reached his teenage years the younger child stopped being as helpful around the house. However, education may be a [confounder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confounder "Confounder") affecting both the father's attitude and the siblings' behavior, and the mother's attitudes did not have a noticeable impact.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-McHale99-61)

## Westermarck effect

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sibling&action=edit&section=27 "Edit section: Westermarck effect")]

Anthropologist [Edvard Westermarck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edvard_Westermarck "Edvard Westermarck") found that children who are brought up together as siblings are desensitized to [sexual attraction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_attraction "Sexual attraction") to one another later in life. This is known as the [Westermarck Effect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westermarck_Effect "Westermarck Effect"). It can be seen in biological and adoptive families, but also in other situations where children are brought up in close contact, such as the [Israeli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel "Israel")[kibbutz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kibbutz "Kibbutz") system and the Chinese [shim-pua marriage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shim-pua_marriage "Shim-pua marriage").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-62)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-63)

The primary word under consideration in this chapter is sibling, which during the Old English period referred simply to a relation, not necessarily to a brother or sister, as in the modern use of the term. The last recorded use in the Oxford English Dictionary in the relative sense is in 1425. There are no records at all of the word for the next 500 years, although its derivational base sib remained in use throughout those years. It was in fact the term sib which, when employed specifically in the fields of anthropology and genetics, gave rise to the readoption of sibling. Sibling, in the narrower modern sense of describing the relationship between two people sharing a common parent, filled a semantic gap in the English lexicon, as there previously was no term to describe the fraternal relationship that did not specify gender. It is clear from early uses of sibling in the 20th century that the writer did not expect the reader to be familiar with the word, as the translator's note from a German eugenics book, Human Heredity explains, 'The word "sib" or "sibling" is coming into use in genetics in the English-speaking world, as an equivalent of the convenient German term "Geschwister" and as a general name for all children born of the same parents, that is to say, to denote brothers and sisters without distinction of sex.' (Baur 1931: 508 in sibling, OED). Likewise, an article in the journal Biometrika from 1903 contains the clarification, '"siblings"=brothers or sisters,' when employing the term. Thus we observe an interesting phenomenon of a native English word being reintroduced to native English speakers, who clearly have no knowledge of it.

A **sibling** is a relative that shares at least one [parent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parent "Parent") with the other person. A [male](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Male "Male") sibling is a [brother](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brother "Brother"), and a [female](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Female "Female") sibling is a [sister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sister "Sister"). A person with no siblings is an [only child](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Only_child "Only child").

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/16/Me_and_my_other_brother.jpg/250px-Me_and_my_other_brother.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Me_and_my_other_brother.jpg)

A [sister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sister "Sister") (female sibling) carrying her [brother](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brother "Brother") (male sibling).

While some circumstances can cause siblings to be raised separately (such as [foster care](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foster_care "Foster care") or [adoption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adoption "Adoption")), most societies have siblings grow up together. This causes the development of strong [emotional bonds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_bonding "Human bonding"), with siblinghood considered a unique type of relationship. The emotional bond between siblings is often complicated and is influenced by factors such as parental treatment, [birth order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_order "Birth order"), [personality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personality_psychology "Personality psychology"), and personal experiences outside the family.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-psychtoday-1)

Medically, a full-sibling is a [first-degree relative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First-degree_relative "First-degree relative") and a half-sibling is a [second-degree relative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second-degree_relative "Second-degree relative") as they are related by 50% and 25%, respectively.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-sibling#cite_note-3)

## Definitions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sibling&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Definitions")]

[![Image 6: icon](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/99/Question_book-new.svg/60px-Question_book-new.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Question_book-new.svg)This section **needs [more citations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability "Wikipedia:Verifiability")**.
