## Themes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Primer_(film)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Themes")]

Although one of the more fantastical elements of science fiction is central to the film, Carruth's goal was to portray scientific discovery in a down-to-earth and realistic manner. He notes that many of the greatest breakthrough scientific discoveries in history have [occurred by accident](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Role_of_chance_in_scientific_discoveries "Role of chance in scientific discoveries"), in locations no more glamorous than Aaron's garage.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-QA-8)

> Whether it involved the history of the number [zero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zero "Zero") or the invention of the [transistor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transistor "Transistor"), two things stood out to me. First is that the discovery that turns out to be the most valuable is usually dismissed as a side-effect. Second is that prototypes almost never include neon lights and chrome. I wanted to see a story play out that was more in line with the way real innovation takes place than I had seen on film before.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-QA-8)

Carruth has said he intended the central theme of the film to be the breakdown of Abe and Aaron's relationship,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-about-com-9) as a result of their inability to cope with the power afforded them by this technological advancement:

> First thing, I saw these guys as scientifically accomplished but ethically, morons. They never had any reasons before to have ethical questions. So when they're hit with this device they're blindsided by it. The first thing they do is make money with it. They're not talking about the ethics of altering your former self.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-indiewire-2)

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Primer_(film)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Production")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/ba/Feynman_EP_Annihilation.svg/250px-Feynman_EP_Annihilation.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Feynman_EP_Annihilation.svg)

This [Feynman diagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feynman_diagram "Feynman diagram"), with time progressing upwards, represents an [electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron "Electron") and [positron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Positron "Positron")[annihilating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annihilation "Annihilation") each other to produce a pair of [photons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photon "Photon"). The electron is represented by an arrow pointing forwards in time, and the positron by one pointing backwards in time. This representation is motivated by [CPT symmetry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CPT_symmetry "CPT symmetry"), which also motivates ideas such as the [one-electron universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One-electron_universe "One-electron universe").

While writing the script, Carruth studied physics to help him make Abe and Aaron's technical dialogue sound authentic. He took the unusual step of eschewing contrived exposition and tried instead to portray the shorthand phrases and jargon used by working scientists. This philosophy carried over into [production design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Production_designer "Production designer"). The time machine itself is a plain gray box, with a distinctive electronic "hum" created by overlaying the sounds of a mechanical grinder and a car engine, rather than by using a processed [digital effect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_audio "Digital audio"). Carruth also set the story in unglamorous industrial parks and suburban tract homes.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-story-prod-4) The principles of time travel in the film are inspired by [Feynman diagrams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feynman_diagram "Feynman diagram"). Carruth explained: "[Richard Feynman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Feynman "Richard Feynman") has some interesting ideas about time. When you look at Feynman diagrams [which map the interaction of elementary particles], there's really no difference between watching an interaction happen forward and backward in time."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-village-voice-interview-10)

Carruth chose to deliberately obfuscate the film's plot to mirror the complexity and confusion created by time travel. As he said in a 2004 interview: "This machine and Abe and Aaron's experience are inherently complicated so it needed to be that way in order for the audience to be where Abe and Aaron are, which was always my hope."[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-about-com-9)

### Filming

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Primer_(film)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Filming")]

[Principal photography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_photography "Principal photography") took place over five weeks, on the outskirts of [Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas "Dallas"), Texas.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-story-prod-4) The film was produced on a budget of only $7000 (equivalent to $12,500 in 2025),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-indiewire-2) and a skeleton crew of five. Carruth acted as writer, director, producer, cinematographer, editor, and music composer. He also stars in the film as Aaron, and many of the other characters are played by his friends and family. The small budget required conservative use of the [Super 16mm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/16_mm_film "16 mm film") filmstock:[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-story-prod-4) the carefully limited number of takes resulted in an extremely low [shooting ratio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shooting_ratio "Shooting ratio") of 2:1. Every shot in the film was meticulously [storyboarded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storyboard "Storyboard") on 35 mm stills.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-about-com-9) Carruth created a distinctive flat, overexposed look for the film by using fluorescent lighting, non-neutral color temperatures, high-speed film stock, and filters.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-story-prod-4)

After shooting, Carruth took two years to fully [post-produce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-production "Post-production")_Primer_. He has since said that this experience was so arduous that he almost abandoned the film on several occasions.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-about-com-9)

### Music

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Primer_(film)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Music")]

The entire [film score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_score "Film score") was created by Carruth. On October 8, 2004, the _Primer_ score was released on [Amazon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_(company) "Amazon (company)")[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-11) and [iTunes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITunes "ITunes").

## Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Primer_(film)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Release")]

### Distribution

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Primer_(film)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Distribution")]

Carruth secured a North American distribution deal with [THINKFilm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/THINKFilm "THINKFilm") after the company's head of [theatrical distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_distributor "Film distributor"), [Mark Urman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Urman "Mark Urman"), saw the film at the [2004 Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Sundance_Film_Festival "2004 Sundance Film Festival").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-filmcomment-12) Although he and Carruth made a "handshake agreement" during the festival, Urman reported that the actual negotiation of the deal was the longest he had ever been involved with, in part due to Carruth's specific demands over how much control over the film he would retain.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-filmcomment-12) The film went on to take $545,436 at the box office.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-13)

### Critical reception and legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Primer_(film)&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Critical reception and legacy")]

_Primer_ received positive reception from critics. [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes") gave the film a 72% approval rating based on 129 reviews, with an average rating of 6.6/10. The consensus reads: "Dense, obtuse, but stimulating, _Primer_ is a film for viewers ready for a cerebral challenge."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-14) The site also listed _Primer_ as one of the best science fiction films "for the thinking man".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-15) On [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), the film holds a score of 68 out of 100 based on reviews from 25 critics, indicating "generally favorable reviews".[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-metacritic-16)

Many reviewers were impressed by the film's originality. Dennis Lim of _[The Village Voice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Village\_Voice "The Village Voice")_ said that it was "the freshest thing the genre has seen since _[2001](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001:\_A\_Space\_Odyssey\_(film) "2001: A Space Odyssey (film)")_",[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-17) while in _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_, [A. O. Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A._O._Scott "A. O. Scott") wrote that Carruth had "the skill, the guile and the seriousness to turn a creaky philosophical gimmick into a dense and troubling moral puzzle".[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-NYT-18) Scott also enjoyed the film's realistic depiction of scientists at work, saying that Carruth had an "impressive feel for the odd, quiet rhythms of small-scale research and development".[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-NYT-18)[Roger Ebert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Ebert "Roger Ebert")'s 3.5 star review for the _Chicago-Sun Times_ also praised the complex technical dialogue as helping viewers feel as if they were eavesdropping on a genuine conversation (if only half-understood by much of the audience) rather than hearing actors delivering [exposition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exposition_(narrative) "Exposition (narrative)").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-Ebert-19)

There was also praise for Carruth's ability to maintain high production values on a minuscule budget, with Ebert declaring: "The movie never looks cheap, because every shot looks as it must look."[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-Ebert-19)[Ty Burr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ty_Burr "Ty Burr") of _[The Boston Globe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Boston\_Globe "The Boston Globe")_ commented that "aspects of _Primer_ are so low-rent as to evoke [guffaws](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guffaw "Guffaw")", but added that "the homemade feel is part of the point".[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-20) Similarly, _[Wired](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wired\_(magazine) "Wired (magazine)")_ wrote: "_Primer_ was noted for its originality – the film takes on complex topics like quantum physics and doesn't dumb them down for the viewer, instead using real jargon and terms that real-life researchers would – and for its commitment to a lo-fi aesthetic. Much of the film is set in garages and car parks, and then with the exception of the two lead roles, every other character is played by a friend or family member of the cast."[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-21)

The film's experimental plot and dense dialogue were controversially received. _[Esquire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esquire\_(magazine) "Esquire (magazine)")_'s Mike D'Angelo claimed that "anybody who claims he fully understands what's going on in _Primer_ after seeing it just once is either a [savant](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/savant "wikt:savant") or a liar".[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-esquire-22) Scott Tobias writes for _[The A.V. Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_A.V.\_Club "The A.V. Club")_: "The banter is heavy on technical jargon and almost perversely short on exposition; were it not for the presence of voiceover narration, the film would be close to incomprehensible."[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-onion-av-5) For the _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los\_Angeles\_Times "Los Angeles Times")_, Carina Chocano writes: "sticklers for linear storytelling are bound to be frustrated by narrative threads that start promisingly, then just sort of fall off the spool".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-23) Ebert predicted _Primer_ would be rejected by those who want lighthearted entertainment, but embraced by the likes of "nerds, geeks, brainiacs [and] Academic Decathlon winners" who would enjoy the film's complexities. Some reviewers were entirely put off by the film's obfuscated narrative. Kirk Honeycutt of _[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hollywood\_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")_ complained that _Primer_ "nearly gets lost in a miasma of technical jargon and scientific conjecture".[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-24)

"_Primer_ is hopelessly confusing and grows more and more byzantine as it unravels", [Chuck Klosterman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuck_Klosterman "Chuck Klosterman") writes in an essay on time travel films five years later. "I've watched it seven or eight times and I still don't know what happened." He nonetheless says it is "the finest movie about time travel I've ever seen" because of its realism:

> It's not that the time machine ... seems more realistic; it's that the time travelers themselves seem more believable. They talk and act (and _think_) like the kind of people who might accidentally figure out how to move through time, which is why it's the best depiction we have of the ethical quandaries that might result from such a discovery.

Ultimately, Klosterman says, the lesson of _Primer_ regarding time travel is that "it's too important to use only for money, but too dangerous to use for anything else".[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-Klosterman_essay-25)

The American director [Steven Soderbergh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Soderbergh "Steven Soderbergh") is regarded as a fan of the film.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-27)

The film has been selected to be part of _[The A.V. Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_A.V.\_Club "The A.V. Club")_'s New Cult Canon.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-onion-av-5) Donald Clarke, film critic with _[The Irish Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Irish\_Times "The Irish Times")_, included _Primer_ at No. 20 on his list of the top twenty films of the decade (2000–2010).[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-29) The film was selected by [_Time_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_(magazine) "Time (magazine)") as one of the Top 10 Time-Travel Movies.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-30) It was ranked number two in _[Popular Mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular\_Mechanics "Popular Mechanics")'_ list of The 30 Best Time Travel Movies.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-31)_[MovieWeb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MovieWeb "MovieWeb")_ ranked _Primer_ at No. 17 on their list of the 30 Best Sci-fi Thrillers Of All Time.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-32)_[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ ranked the film at No. 25 on their list of "The Top 40 Sci-Fi Movies of the 21st Century".[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-33) Science fiction author [Greg Egan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Egan "Greg Egan") describes _Primer_ as "an ingenious, tautly constructed time-travel story".[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-34)

_**Primer**_ is a 2004 American [independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_film "Independent film")[science fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_fiction "Science fiction") film written, directed, produced, edited, and scored by Shane Carruth in his feature debut. The film stars Carruth and [David Sullivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Sullivan_(actor) "David Sullivan (actor)"), and depicts the events surrounding the accidental discovery of [time travel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_travel "Time travel").

_Primer_ is noted for its extremely low budget, experimental plot structure, philosophical implications, and complex technical dialogue, which Carruth, a college graduate with a degree in mathematics and a former engineer, chose not to simplify for the sake of the audience.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-story-prod-4) The film won the [Grand Jury Prize Dramatic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Jury_Prize_Dramatic "Grand Jury Prize Dramatic") at the [2004 Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Sundance_Film_Festival "2004 Sundance Film Festival"), before securing a limited release in the United States, and has since gained a [cult following](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cult_following "Cult following").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-onion-av-5)

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Primer_(film)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/84/Time_Travel_Method-2.svg/250px-Time_Travel_Method-2.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Time_Travel_Method-2.svg)

The operation of time travel in _Primer_.

Two engineers, Aaron and Abe, supplement their day jobs with entrepreneurial tech projects, working out of Aaron's garage. During one such research effort involving electromagnetic reduction of objects' weight, the two men accidentally discover an 'A-to-B' [causal loop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Causal_loop "Causal loop") side-effect: objects left in the weight-reducing field exhibit temporal anomalies, proceeding normally (from time 'A,' when the field was activated, to time 'B,' when the field is powered off), then backward (from 'B' back to 'A') in a continuously repeating sequence, such that objects can leave the field in the present, or at some previous point.

Abe refines this proof-of-concept and builds a stable time-apparatus ("the box"), sized to accommodate a human subject. Abe uses this box to travel six hours into his own past—as part of this process, Abe stays in a hotel room, isolating himself from any communication with the outside world, so as not to interact or interfere with the outside world, after which he enters the box then waits inside for six hours (thus going back in time six hours). Once he exits the box, Abe travels across town, explains the proceedings to Aaron, and brings Aaron back to the self-storage facility housing the box. At the facility, they watch the earlier version of Abe enter the box.

Abe and Aaron repeat Abe's six-hour experiment multiple times over multiple days, making profitable same-day stock trades armed with foreknowledge of the market's performance. The duo's divergent personalities–Abe cautious and controlling, Aaron impulsive and meddlesome–put subtle strain on their collaboration and friendship. Additionally, the time travel is taxing on Abe and Aaron's bodies: effectively their days become 36 hours long when including the extra time afforded by the box. As the film progresses, the two men begin to notice alarming side effects of time travel which take the form of earbleeds. Later, they notice their handwriting progressively worsening.

The tension between Abe and Aaron comes to a head after a late-night encounter with Thomas Granger (father to Abe's girlfriend, Rachel), who appears inexplicably unshaven and exists in overlap with his original suburban self. Granger falls into a comatose state after being pursued by Aaron; Aaron theorizes that, at some unknown point in the future, Granger entered the "box", with timeline-altering consequences. Abe concludes that time travel is simply too dangerous and enters a secret second box (the "failsafe box", built before the experiment began and kept continuously running), traveling back four days to prevent the experiment's launch.

Future-Abe sedates Original-Abe (so he will never conduct the initial time travel experiment) and meets Aaron at a park bench so as to dissuade him, but finds that Future-Aaron has gotten there first. It is revealed that during the initial experiment, Aaron had accidentally discovered the failsafe and used it, bringing a folded up box back into the past with his own body to set up his own failsafe and stay one step ahead of Abe; Future-Aaron then drugged his original self and locked him in his attic to keep him from interfering. Aaron then proceeded to record all the conversations of the following days with an inconspicuous earpiece, in order to be able to replay events and conversations in case something went wrong. Future-Abe faints at this revelation, overcome by shock and fatigue.

The two men briefly and tentatively reconcile. They jointly travel back in time, experiencing and reshaping an event where Abe's girlfriend Rachel was nearly killed by a gun-wielding party crasher. After many repetitions, Aaron, forearmed with knowledge of the party's events, stops the gunman, becoming a local hero. Abe and Aaron ultimately part ways; Aaron considers a new life in foreign countries where he can tamper more broadly for personal gain, while Abe states his intent to remain in town and dissuade/sabotage the original "box" experiment. Abe warns Aaron to leave and never return.

Multiple "box-aware" versions of Aaron circulate—at least one Future-Aaron has shared his knowledge with Original-Aaron, via a phone call that serves as the film's narration. Future-Abe watches over Original-Abe, going to painstaking extremes to keep him and Original-Aaron unaware of the future. An Aaron directs French-speaking workers in the construction of a warehouse-sized box.

*   Shane Carruth as Aaron
*   [David Sullivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Sullivan_(actor) "David Sullivan (actor)") as Abe

Carruth cast himself as Aaron after having trouble finding actors who could "break ... the habit of filling each line with so much drama".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-story-prod-4) Most of the other actors are either friends or family members.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-tech_support-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-itl-7)

## Themes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Primer_(film)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Themes")]

Although one of the more fantastical elements of science fiction is central to the film, Carruth's goal was to portray scientific discovery in a down-to-earth and realistic manner. He notes that many of the greatest breakthrough scientific discoveries in history have [occurred by accident](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Role_of_chance_in_scientific_discoveries "Role of chance in scientific discoveries"), in locations no more glamorous than Aaron's garage.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-QA-8)

> Whether it involved the history of the number [zero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zero "Zero") or the invention of the [transistor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transistor "Transistor"), two things stood out to me. First is that the discovery that turns out to be the most valuable is usually dismissed as a side-effect. Second is that prototypes almost never include neon lights and chrome. I wanted to see a story play out that was more in line with the way real innovation takes place than I had seen on film before.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-QA-8)

Carruth has said he intended the central theme of the film to be the breakdown of Abe and Aaron's relationship,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-about-com-9) as a result of their inability to cope with the power afforded them by this technological advancement:

> First thing, I saw these guys as scientifically accomplished but ethically, morons. They never had any reasons before to have ethical questions. So when they're hit with this device they're blindsided by it. The first thing they do is make money with it. They're not talking about the ethics of altering your former self.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-indiewire-2)

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Primer_(film)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Production")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/ba/Feynman_EP_Annihilation.svg/250px-Feynman_EP_Annihilation.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Feynman_EP_Annihilation.svg)

This [Feynman diagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feynman_diagram "Feynman diagram"), with time progressing upwards, represents an [electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron "Electron") and [positron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Positron "Positron")[annihilating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annihilation "Annihilation") each other to produce a pair of [photons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photon "Photon"). The electron is represented by an arrow pointing forwards in time, and the positron by one pointing backwards in time. This representation is motivated by [CPT symmetry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CPT_symmetry "CPT symmetry"), which also motivates ideas such as the [one-electron universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One-electron_universe "One-electron universe").

While writing the script, Carruth studied physics to help him make Abe and Aaron's technical dialogue sound authentic. He took the unusual step of eschewing contrived exposition and tried instead to portray the shorthand phrases and jargon used by working scientists. This philosophy carried over into [production design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Production_designer "Production designer"). The time machine itself is a plain gray box, with a distinctive electronic "hum" created by overlaying the sounds of a mechanical grinder and a car engine, rather than by using a processed [digital effect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_audio "Digital audio"). Carruth also set the story in unglamorous industrial parks and suburban tract homes.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-story-prod-4) The principles of time travel in the film are inspired by [Feynman diagrams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feynman_diagram "Feynman diagram"). Carruth explained: "[Richard Feynman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Feynman "Richard Feynman") has some interesting ideas about time. When you look at Feynman diagrams [which map the interaction of elementary particles], there's really no difference between watching an interaction happen forward and backward in time."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-village-voice-interview-10)

Carruth chose to deliberately obfuscate the film's plot to mirror the complexity and confusion created by time travel. As he said in a 2004 interview: "This machine and Abe and Aaron's experience are inherently complicated so it needed to be that way in order for the audience to be where Abe and Aaron are, which was always my hope."[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-about-com-9)

### Filming

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Primer_(film)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Filming")]

[Principal photography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_photography "Principal photography") took place over five weeks, on the outskirts of [Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas "Dallas"), Texas.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-story-prod-4) The film was produced on a budget of only $7000 (equivalent to $12,500 in 2025),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-indiewire-2) and a skeleton crew of five. Carruth acted as writer, director, producer, cinematographer, editor, and music composer. He also stars in the film as Aaron, and many of the other characters are played by his friends and family. The small budget required conservative use of the [Super 16mm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/16_mm_film "16 mm film") filmstock:[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-story-prod-4) the carefully limited number of takes resulted in an extremely low [shooting ratio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shooting_ratio "Shooting ratio") of 2:1. Every shot in the film was meticulously [storyboarded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storyboard "Storyboard") on 35 mm stills.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-about-com-9) Carruth created a distinctive flat, overexposed look for the film by using fluorescent lighting, non-neutral color temperatures, high-speed film stock, and filters.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-story-prod-4)

After shooting, Carruth took two years to fully [post-produce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-production "Post-production")_Primer_. He has since said that this experience was so arduous that he almost abandoned the film on several occasions.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-about-com-9)

### Music

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Primer_(film)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Music")]

The entire [film score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_score "Film score") was created by Carruth. On October 8, 2004, the _Primer_ score was released on [Amazon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_(company) "Amazon (company)")[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-11) and [iTunes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITunes "ITunes").

## Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Primer_(film)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Release")]

### Distribution

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Primer_(film)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Distribution")]

Carruth secured a North American distribution deal with [THINKFilm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/THINKFilm "THINKFilm") after the company's head of [theatrical distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_distributor "Film distributor"), [Mark Urman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Urman "Mark Urman"), saw the film at the [2004 Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Sundance_Film_Festival "2004 Sundance Film Festival").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-filmcomment-12) Although he and Carruth made a "handshake agreement" during the festival, Urman reported that the actual negotiation of the deal was the longest he had ever been involved with, in part due to Carruth's specific demands over how much control over the film he would retain.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-filmcomment-12) The film went on to take $545,436 at the box office.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-13)

### Critical reception and legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Primer_(film)&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Critical reception and legacy")]

_Primer_ received positive reception from critics. [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes") gave the film a 72% approval rating based on 129 reviews, with an average rating of 6.6/10. The consensus reads: "Dense, obtuse, but stimulating, _Primer_ is a film for viewers ready for a cerebral challenge."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-14) The site also listed _Primer_ as one of the best science fiction films "for the thinking man".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-15) On [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), the film holds a score of 68 out of 100 based on reviews from 25 critics, indicating "generally favorable reviews".[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-metacritic-16)

Many reviewers were impressed by the film's originality. Dennis Lim of _[The Village Voice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Village\_Voice "The Village Voice")_ said that it was "the freshest thing the genre has seen since _[2001](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001:\_A\_Space\_Odyssey\_(film) "2001: A Space Odyssey (film)")_",[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-17) while in _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_, [A. O. Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A._O._Scott "A. O. Scott") wrote that Carruth had "the skill, the guile and the seriousness to turn a creaky philosophical gimmick into a dense and troubling moral puzzle".[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-NYT-18) Scott also enjoyed the film's realistic depiction of scientists at work, saying that Carruth had an "impressive feel for the odd, quiet rhythms of small-scale research and development".[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-NYT-18)[Roger Ebert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Ebert "Roger Ebert")'s 3.5 star review for the _Chicago-Sun Times_ also praised the complex technical dialogue as helping viewers feel as if they were eavesdropping on a genuine conversation (if only half-understood by much of the audience) rather than hearing actors delivering [exposition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exposition_(narrative) "Exposition (narrative)").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-Ebert-19)

There was also praise for Carruth's ability to maintain high production values on a minuscule budget, with Ebert declaring: "The movie never looks cheap, because every shot looks as it must look."[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-Ebert-19)[Ty Burr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ty_Burr "Ty Burr") of _[The Boston Globe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Boston\_Globe "The Boston Globe")_ commented that "aspects of _Primer_ are so low-rent as to evoke [guffaws](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guffaw "Guffaw")", but added that "the homemade feel is part of the point".[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-20) Similarly, _[Wired](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wired\_(magazine) "Wired (magazine)")_ wrote: "_Primer_ was noted for its originality – the film takes on complex topics like quantum physics and doesn't dumb them down for the viewer, instead using real jargon and terms that real-life researchers would – and for its commitment to a lo-fi aesthetic. Much of the film is set in garages and car parks, and then with the exception of the two lead roles, every other character is played by a friend or family member of the cast."[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-21)

The film's experimental plot and dense dialogue were controversially received. _[Esquire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esquire\_(magazine) "Esquire (magazine)")_'s Mike D'Angelo claimed that "anybody who claims he fully understands what's going on in _Primer_ after seeing it just once is either a [savant](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/savant "wikt:savant") or a liar".[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-esquire-22) Scott Tobias writes for _[The A.V. Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_A.V.\_Club "The A.V. Club")_: "The banter is heavy on technical jargon and almost perversely short on exposition; were it not for the presence of voiceover narration, the film would be close to incomprehensible."[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-onion-av-5) For the _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los\_Angeles\_Times "Los Angeles Times")_, Carina Chocano writes: "sticklers for linear storytelling are bound to be frustrated by narrative threads that start promisingly, then just sort of fall off the spool".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-23) Ebert predicted _Primer_ would be rejected by those who want lighthearted entertainment, but embraced by the likes of "nerds, geeks, brainiacs [and] Academic Decathlon winners" who would enjoy the film's complexities. Some reviewers were entirely put off by the film's obfuscated narrative. Kirk Honeycutt of _[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hollywood\_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")_ complained that _Primer_ "nearly gets lost in a miasma of technical jargon and scientific conjecture".[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-24)

"_Primer_ is hopelessly confusing and grows more and more byzantine as it unravels", [Chuck Klosterman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuck_Klosterman "Chuck Klosterman") writes in an essay on time travel films five years later. "I've watched it seven or eight times and I still don't know what happened." He nonetheless says it is "the finest movie about time travel I've ever seen" because of its realism:

> It's not that the time machine ... seems more realistic; it's that the time travelers themselves seem more believable. They talk and act (and _think_) like the kind of people who might accidentally figure out how to move through time, which is why it's the best depiction we have of the ethical quandaries that might result from such a discovery.

Ultimately, Klosterman says, the lesson of _Primer_ regarding time travel is that "it's too important to use only for money, but too dangerous to use for anything else".[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-Klosterman_essay-25)

The American director [Steven Soderbergh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Soderbergh "Steven Soderbergh") is regarded as a fan of the film.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-27)

The film has been selected to be part of _[The A.V. Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_A.V.\_Club "The A.V. Club")_'s New Cult Canon.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-onion-av-5) Donald Clarke, film critic with _[The Irish Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Irish\_Times "The Irish Times")_, included _Primer_ at No. 20 on his list of the top twenty films of the decade (2000–2010).[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-29) The film was selected by [_Time_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_(magazine) "Time (magazine)") as one of the Top 10 Time-Travel Movies.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-30) It was ranked number two in _[Popular Mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular\_Mechanics "Popular Mechanics")'_ list of The 30 Best Time Travel Movies.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-31)_[MovieWeb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MovieWeb "MovieWeb")_ ranked _Primer_ at No. 17 on their list of the 30 Best Sci-fi Thrillers Of All Time.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-32)_[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ ranked the film at No. 25 on their list of "The Top 40 Sci-Fi Movies of the 21st Century".[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-33) Science fiction author [Greg Egan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Egan "Greg Egan") describes _Primer_ as "an ingenious, tautly constructed time-travel story".[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primer_(film)#cite_note-34)

**Channing Matthew Tatum** (born April 26, 1980) is an American actor and film producer. He made his film debut in the drama _[Coach Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coach\_Carter "Coach Carter")_ (2005), and had his [breakthrough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breakthrough_role "Breakthrough role") with the sports comedy film _[She's the Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/She's\_the\_Man "She's the Man")_ (2006) and the dance film _[Step Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Step\_Up\_(film) "Step Up (film)")_ (2006). He rose to prominence for playing [Duke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duke_(G.I._Joe) "Duke (G.I. Joe)") in the action films _[G.I. Joe: The Rise of Cobra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G.I.\_Joe:\_The\_Rise\_of\_Cobra "G.I. Joe: The Rise of Cobra")_ (2009) and _[G.I. Joe: Retaliation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G.I.\_Joe:\_Retaliation "G.I. Joe: Retaliation")_ (2013), the title role in the comedy-drama films _[Magic Mike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic\_Mike "Magic Mike")_ (2012), _[Magic Mike XXL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic\_Mike\_XXL "Magic Mike XXL")_ (2015) and _[Magic Mike's Last Dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic\_Mike's\_Last\_Dance "Magic Mike's Last Dance")_ (2023), and an undercover cop in the action-comedy films _[21 Jump Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21\_Jump\_Street\_(film) "21 Jump Street (film)")_ (2012) and _[22 Jump Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/22\_Jump\_Street "22 Jump Street")_ (2014).

Tatum's other films include _[The Vow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Vow\_(2012\_film) "The Vow (2012 film)")_ (2012), _[White House Down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White\_House\_Down "White House Down")_ (2013), _[Foxcatcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foxcatcher "Foxcatcher")_ (2014), _[The Hateful Eight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hateful\_Eight "The Hateful Eight")_ (2015), _[Hail, Caesar!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hail,\_Caesar! "Hail, Caesar!")_ (2016), _[Logan Lucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logan\_Lucky "Logan Lucky")_ (2017), _[The Lost City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lost\_City\_(2022\_film) "The Lost City (2022 film)")_ (2022), and _[Deadpool & Wolverine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadpool\_&\_Wolverine "Deadpool & Wolverine")_ (2024). He has produced several of his films, including the [road movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_movie "Road movie")_[Dog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dog\_(2022\_film) "Dog (2022 film)")_ (2022), which he also starred in and co-directed. He was listed as one of _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")_'s [100 most influential people in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_100 "Time 100") in 2022.

## Early life and education

Channing Matthew Tatum was born on April 26, 1980,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-2) in [Cullman, Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cullman,_Alabama "Cullman, Alabama"), to Kay Tatum (née Faust), an airline worker, and Glenn Tatum, a construction worker.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-engaged-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-4) He has a sister named Paige. He is of Irish, French, and German ancestry.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-5) His family moved to [Gautier, Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gautier,_Mississippi "Gautier, Mississippi"), in the [Pascagoula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pascagoula,_Mississippi "Pascagoula, Mississippi") area, when he was six. Until he was ten years old, he lived in a rural setting near the [bayous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bayou "Bayou") along the [Pascagoula River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pascagoula_River "Pascagoula River").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-hometowns-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-7)

Tatum has discussed having dealt with [attention deficit disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attention_deficit_disorder "Attention deficit disorder") (ADD) and [dyslexia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dyslexia "Dyslexia") while growing up, which affected his ability to do well in school.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-8) In his youth, Tatum participated in [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football"), soccer, track, baseball, and [wuzuquan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wuzuquan "Wuzuquan")[kung fu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_martial_arts "Chinese martial arts").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-9)

Tatum spent most of his teenage years in the [Tampa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa,_Florida "Tampa, Florida") area, where he initially attended [Gaither High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaither_High_School "Gaither High School"). His parents wanted more effort and gave him the option of selecting a private high school or attending a military school; he chose [Tampa Catholic High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa_Catholic_High_School "Tampa Catholic High School"), where he graduated in 1998 and was voted most athletic.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-10) He later attended [Glenville State College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenville_State_College "Glenville State College") in [Glenville, West Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenville,_West_Virginia "Glenville, West Virginia") on a football scholarship, but dropped out.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-producer-11)

_[Us Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Us\_Weekly "Us Weekly")_ reported that around this time Tatum left his job as a roofer and began working as a [stripper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Male_stripper "Male stripper") at a local [nightclub](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strip_club "Strip club") under the name "Chan Crawford".[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-buds-13) In 2010, he told an Australian newspaper that he wanted to make a film about his experiences as a stripper.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-14) That idea led to the film _[Magic Mike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic\_Mike "Magic Mike")_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-buds-13)

## Career

### 2000s

In 2000, Tatum was first cast as a dancer in [Ricky Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Martin "Ricky Martin")'s "[She Bangs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/She_Bangs "She Bangs")" music video,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-Allmovie-15) after an audition in [Orlando, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando,_Florida "Orlando, Florida"); he was paid $400 for the job. His experience in the fashion industry began as a model working for noted clients such as [Armani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armani "Armani") and [Abercrombie & Fitch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abercrombie_&_Fitch "Abercrombie & Fitch"). He soon moved into television commercials, landing national spots for [Mountain Dew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mountain_Dew "Mountain Dew") and [Pepsi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepsi "Pepsi") in 2002. He subsequently signed with Page 305 (Page Parkes Modeling Agency), a modeling agency in [Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami "Miami"). He was cast by Al David for _[Vogue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vogue\_(magazine) "Vogue (magazine)")_ magazine and soon after appeared in campaigns for [Abercrombie & Fitch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abercrombie_&_Fitch "Abercrombie & Fitch"), [Nautica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nautica_(clothing_company) "Nautica (clothing company)"), [Dolce & Gabbana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolce_&_Gabbana "Dolce & Gabbana"), [American Eagle Outfitters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Eagle_Outfitters "American Eagle Outfitters"), and [Emporio Armani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emporio_Armani "Emporio Armani"). He was picked as one of _Tear Sheet_ magazine's "50 Most Beautiful Faces" of October 2001. Tatum signed with [Ford Models](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_Models "Ford Models") in New York City.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-16)

Tatum in 2009

In 2006, Tatum starred in _[She's The Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/She's\_The\_Man "She's The Man")_ opposite [Amanda Bynes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amanda_Bynes "Amanda Bynes"), which was named "the greatest Shakespeare adaptation since '10 Things I Hate About You'" by _[Business Insider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business\_Insider "Business Insider")_.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-17) Later that year, Tatum starred opposite his future wife [Jenna Dewan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan "Jenna Dewan") in _[Step Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Step\_Up\_(film) "Step Up (film)")_, which was his breakout role. Although it was widely panned, it has earned $115 million worldwide.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-stonebest-18)

In 2008, Tatum co-starred in director [Kimberly Peirce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kimberly_Peirce "Kimberly Peirce")'s film _[Stop-Loss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stop-Loss\_(film) "Stop-Loss (film)")_, about soldiers returning home from the [Iraq War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq_War "Iraq War"), and in director [Stuart Townsend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stuart_Townsend "Stuart Townsend")'s film _[Battle in Seattle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle\_in\_Seattle "Battle in Seattle")_, about the 1999 protest of the [World Trade Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Trade_Organization "World Trade Organization") meeting in [Seattle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle "Seattle"). Tatum played in the short film _The Trap_, directed by [Rita Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Wilson "Rita Wilson").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-19)

Tatum and [Dito Montiel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dito_Montiel "Dito Montiel"), who worked together on _[A Guide to Recognizing Your Saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Guide\_to\_Recognizing\_Your\_Saints "A Guide to Recognizing Your Saints")_, reteamed on the action drama _[Fighting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fighting\_(2009\_film) "Fighting (2009 film)")_ for [Rogue Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogue_Pictures "Rogue Pictures"). He starred as Shawn MacArthur, a young man who starts out selling counterfeit goods in New York City. He next appeared in writer/director/producer [Michael Mann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Mann_(film_director) "Michael Mann (film director)")'s 2009 crime drama _[Public Enemies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public\_Enemies\_(2009\_film) "Public Enemies (2009 film)")_, playing the 1930s American [gangster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gangster "Gangster")[Pretty Boy Floyd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pretty_Boy_Floyd "Pretty Boy Floyd").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-stonebest-18) The same year, Tatum starred as [Duke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duke_(G.I._Joe) "Duke (G.I. Joe)") in _[G.I. Joe: The Rise of Cobra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G.I.\_Joe:\_The\_Rise\_of\_Cobra "G.I. In 2012, Tatum hosted _[Saturday Night Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday\_Night\_Live "Saturday Night Live")_[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-23) and appeared in four films. He co-starred in [Steven Soderbergh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Soderbergh "Steven Soderbergh")'s action-thriller _[Haywire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haywire\_(2011\_film) "Haywire (2011 film)")_, _[The Vow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Vow\_(2012\_film) "The Vow (2012 film)")_ with [Rachel McAdams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachel_McAdams "Rachel McAdams"), and _[21 Jump Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21\_Jump\_Street\_(film) "21 Jump Street (film)")_ (film adaptation of [TV series of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21_Jump_Street "21 Jump Street")) with [Jonah Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonah_Hill "Jonah Hill").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-24)

## Other ventures

### Business

In October 2012, Tatum and a friend opened the Saints and Sinners burlesque-themed restaurant and bar in New Orleans, which remained open until 2024.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-45)

### Production companies

In an interview with _[Details](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Details\_(magazine) "Details (magazine)")_ magazine, published in early 2012, Tatum said he wants to produce all the films he stars in, "I really don't want to be in any more movies that I don't produce. Unless it's with one of the 10 directors that I really want to work with, I don't have any interest in not being on the ground floor of creating it."[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-46) He, his then-wife [Jenna Dewan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan "Jenna Dewan"), and their production partner [Reid Carolin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reid_Carolin "Reid Carolin") signed a two-year production deal in 2010 with [Relativity Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Relativity_Media "Relativity Media") for any films they may develop during that time.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-47)

Tatum started two production companies, 33andOut Productions[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-48) and Iron Horse Entertainment.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-49) Their first production was the 2010 documentary _[Earth Made of Glass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth\_Made\_of\_Glass\_(film) "Earth Made of Glass (film)")_. In 2021, another one of his production companies, Free Association, signed a first look deal with [MGM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer "Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-50)

### Writing

Tatum has written two picture books inspired by his daughter.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-pmjuneau-51) The first, _The One and Only Sparkella_ (2021), was a #1 [_New York Times_ bestseller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times_Best_Seller_list "The New York Times Best Seller list") for children's picture books the week it published.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-52)_The One and Only Sparkella Makes a Plan_ was published in 2022.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-53)

## Personal life

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fe/Channing_Tatum%2C_Jenna_Dewan_2012.jpg/250px-Channing_Tatum%2C_Jenna_Dewan_2012.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Channing_Tatum,_Jenna_Dewan_2012.jpg)

Tatum and then-wife Jenna Dewan at the [Peabody Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peabody_Awards "Peabody Awards") 2012

In 2006, Tatum met actress [Jenna Dewan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan "Jenna Dewan") on the set of their film _[Step Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Step\_Up\_(film) "Step Up (film)")_, and they married on July 11, 2009, in [Malibu, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malibu,_California "Malibu, California").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-marriage-56) They have one daughter, born in 2013.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-57) On April 2, 2018, the couple announced they were separating.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-58) Six months later, Dewan filed for divorce from Tatum.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-59) The divorce was finalized in November 2019.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-60) In a 2023 interview with _[Vanity Fair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanity\_Fair\_(magazine) "Vanity Fair (magazine)")_, Tatum questioned whether he would ever remarry, though said his divorce prompted self-improvement, including a strong relationship with his daughter.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-pmjuneau-51)

Tatum dated English singer [Jessie J](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessie_J "Jessie J") from 2018 to 2020.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-62)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-63) In 2021, Tatum started dating [Zoë Kravitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zo%C3%AB_Kravitz "Zoë Kravitz") and, by 2023, the couple were [engaged](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engagement "Engagement").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-64)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-65) The engagement was called off in October 2024.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-66) In April 2025, it was confirmed that Tatum is in a relationship with model Inka Williams.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-67)

In February 2026, Tatum suffered a severe shoulder injury that resulted in surgery and him having to drop-out of a film titled _Kockroach._[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-68)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-69)

Tatum is a fan of [anime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anime "Anime"), and has said that he and his daughter, Everly, enjoy watching _[Demon Slayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demon\_Slayer:\_Kimetsu\_no\_Yaiba\_(TV\_series) "Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba (TV series)")_ and _[Black Clover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black\_Clover\_(TV\_series) "Black Clover (TV series)")_.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-70)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-71)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-72)

**Channing Matthew Tatum** (born April 26, 1980) is an American actor and film producer. He made his film debut in the drama _[Coach Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coach\_Carter "Coach Carter")_ (2005), and had his [breakthrough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breakthrough_role "Breakthrough role") with the sports comedy film _[She's the Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/She's\_the\_Man "She's the Man")_ (2006) and the dance film _[Step Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Step\_Up\_(film) "Step Up (film)")_ (2006). He rose to prominence for playing [Duke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duke_(G.I._Joe) "Duke (G.I. Joe)") in the action films _[G.I. Joe: The Rise of Cobra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G.I.\_Joe:\_The\_Rise\_of\_Cobra "G.I. Joe: The Rise of Cobra")_ (2009) and _[G.I. Joe: Retaliation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G.I.\_Joe:\_Retaliation "G.I. Joe: Retaliation")_ (2013), the title role in the comedy-drama films _[Magic Mike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic\_Mike "Magic Mike")_ (2012), _[Magic Mike XXL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic\_Mike\_XXL "Magic Mike XXL")_ (2015) and _[Magic Mike's Last Dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic\_Mike's\_Last\_Dance "Magic Mike's Last Dance")_ (2023), and an undercover cop in the action-comedy films _[21 Jump Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21\_Jump\_Street\_(film) "21 Jump Street (film)")_ (2012) and _[22 Jump Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/22\_Jump\_Street "22 Jump Street")_ (2014).

Tatum's other films include _[The Vow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Vow\_(2012\_film) "The Vow (2012 film)")_ (2012), _[White House Down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White\_House\_Down "White House Down")_ (2013), _[Foxcatcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foxcatcher "Foxcatcher")_ (2014), _[The Hateful Eight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hateful\_Eight "The Hateful Eight")_ (2015), _[Hail, Caesar!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hail,\_Caesar! "Hail, Caesar!")_ (2016), _[Logan Lucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logan\_Lucky "Logan Lucky")_ (2017), _[The Lost City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lost\_City\_(2022\_film) "The Lost City (2022 film)")_ (2022), and _[Deadpool & Wolverine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadpool\_&\_Wolverine "Deadpool & Wolverine")_ (2024). He has produced several of his films, including the [road movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_movie "Road movie")_[Dog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dog\_(2022\_film) "Dog (2022 film)")_ (2022), which he also starred in and co-directed. He was listed as one of _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")_'s [100 most influential people in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_100 "Time 100") in 2022.

## Early life and education

Channing Matthew Tatum was born on April 26, 1980,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-2) in [Cullman, Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cullman,_Alabama "Cullman, Alabama"), to Kay Tatum (née Faust), an airline worker, and Glenn Tatum, a construction worker.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-engaged-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-4) He has a sister named Paige. He is of Irish, French, and German ancestry.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-5) His family moved to [Gautier, Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gautier,_Mississippi "Gautier, Mississippi"), in the [Pascagoula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pascagoula,_Mississippi "Pascagoula, Mississippi") area, when he was six. Until he was ten years old, he lived in a rural setting near the [bayous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bayou "Bayou") along the [Pascagoula River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pascagoula_River "Pascagoula River").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-hometowns-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-7)

Tatum has discussed having dealt with [attention deficit disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attention_deficit_disorder "Attention deficit disorder") (ADD) and [dyslexia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dyslexia "Dyslexia") while growing up, which affected his ability to do well in school.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-8) In his youth, Tatum participated in [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football"), soccer, track, baseball, and [wuzuquan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wuzuquan "Wuzuquan")[kung fu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_martial_arts "Chinese martial arts").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-9)

Tatum spent most of his teenage years in the [Tampa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa,_Florida "Tampa, Florida") area, where he initially attended [Gaither High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaither_High_School "Gaither High School"). His parents wanted more effort and gave him the option of selecting a private high school or attending a military school; he chose [Tampa Catholic High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa_Catholic_High_School "Tampa Catholic High School"), where he graduated in 1998 and was voted most athletic.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-10) He later attended [Glenville State College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenville_State_College "Glenville State College") in [Glenville, West Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenville,_West_Virginia "Glenville, West Virginia") on a football scholarship, but dropped out.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-producer-11)

_[Us Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Us\_Weekly "Us Weekly")_ reported that around this time Tatum left his job as a roofer and began working as a [stripper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Male_stripper "Male stripper") at a local [nightclub](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strip_club "Strip club") under the name "Chan Crawford".[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-buds-13) In 2010, he told an Australian newspaper that he wanted to make a film about his experiences as a stripper.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-14) That idea led to the film _[Magic Mike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic\_Mike "Magic Mike")_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-buds-13)

## Career

### 2000s

In 2000, Tatum was first cast as a dancer in [Ricky Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Martin "Ricky Martin")'s "[She Bangs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/She_Bangs "She Bangs")" music video,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-Allmovie-15) after an audition in [Orlando, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando,_Florida "Orlando, Florida"); he was paid $400 for the job. His experience in the fashion industry began as a model working for noted clients such as [Armani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armani "Armani") and [Abercrombie & Fitch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abercrombie_&_Fitch "Abercrombie & Fitch"). He soon moved into television commercials, landing national spots for [Mountain Dew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mountain_Dew "Mountain Dew") and [Pepsi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepsi "Pepsi") in 2002. He subsequently signed with Page 305 (Page Parkes Modeling Agency), a modeling agency in [Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami "Miami"). He was cast by Al David for _[Vogue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vogue\_(magazine) "Vogue (magazine)")_ magazine and soon after appeared in campaigns for [Abercrombie & Fitch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abercrombie_&_Fitch "Abercrombie & Fitch"), [Nautica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nautica_(clothing_company) "Nautica (clothing company)"), [Dolce & Gabbana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolce_&_Gabbana "Dolce & Gabbana"), [American Eagle Outfitters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Eagle_Outfitters "American Eagle Outfitters"), and [Emporio Armani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emporio_Armani "Emporio Armani"). He was picked as one of _Tear Sheet_ magazine's "50 Most Beautiful Faces" of October 2001. Tatum signed with [Ford Models](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_Models "Ford Models") in New York City.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-16)

Tatum in 2009

In 2006, Tatum starred in _[She's The Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/She's\_The\_Man "She's The Man")_ opposite [Amanda Bynes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amanda_Bynes "Amanda Bynes"), which was named "the greatest Shakespeare adaptation since '10 Things I Hate About You'" by _[Business Insider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business\_Insider "Business Insider")_.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-17) Later that year, Tatum starred opposite his future wife [Jenna Dewan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan "Jenna Dewan") in _[Step Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Step\_Up\_(film) "Step Up (film)")_, which was his breakout role. Although it was widely panned, it has earned $115 million worldwide.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-stonebest-18)

In 2008, Tatum co-starred in director [Kimberly Peirce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kimberly_Peirce "Kimberly Peirce")'s film _[Stop-Loss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stop-Loss\_(film) "Stop-Loss (film)")_, about soldiers returning home from the [Iraq War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq_War "Iraq War"), and in director [Stuart Townsend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stuart_Townsend "Stuart Townsend")'s film _[Battle in Seattle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle\_in\_Seattle "Battle in Seattle")_, about the 1999 protest of the [World Trade Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Trade_Organization "World Trade Organization") meeting in [Seattle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle "Seattle"). Tatum played in the short film _The Trap_, directed by [Rita Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Wilson "Rita Wilson").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-19)

Tatum and [Dito Montiel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dito_Montiel "Dito Montiel"), who worked together on _[A Guide to Recognizing Your Saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Guide\_to\_Recognizing\_Your\_Saints "A Guide to Recognizing Your Saints")_, reteamed on the action drama _[Fighting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fighting\_(2009\_film) "Fighting (2009 film)")_ for [Rogue Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogue_Pictures "Rogue Pictures"). He starred as Shawn MacArthur, a young man who starts out selling counterfeit goods in New York City. He next appeared in writer/director/producer [Michael Mann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Mann_(film_director) "Michael Mann (film director)")'s 2009 crime drama _[Public Enemies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public\_Enemies\_(2009\_film) "Public Enemies (2009 film)")_, playing the 1930s American [gangster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gangster "Gangster")[Pretty Boy Floyd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pretty_Boy_Floyd "Pretty Boy Floyd").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-stonebest-18) The same year, Tatum starred as [Duke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duke_(G.I._Joe) "Duke (G.I. Joe)") in _[G.I. Joe: The Rise of Cobra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G.I.\_Joe:\_The\_Rise\_of\_Cobra "G.I. Joe: The Rise of Cobra")_, [Paramount Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount_Pictures "Paramount Pictures")' live-action film based on the popular [Hasbro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasbro "Hasbro") action figures. He was initially reluctant to take the role as he feared the film would glorify war, but overcame his reluctance after reading the script.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-20) He played a soldier in _[Dear John](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dear\_John\_(2010\_film) "Dear John (2010 film)")_, a film based on the popular [Nicholas Sparks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicholas_Sparks "Nicholas Sparks") bestseller.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-21) He later said that he accepted the role to learn from director [Lasse Hallström](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lasse_Hallstr%C3%B6m "Lasse Hallström") because he never studied at an acting school.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-22)

### 2010s

In 2012, Tatum hosted _[Saturday Night Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday\_Night\_Live "Saturday Night Live")_[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-23) and appeared in four films. He co-starred in [Steven Soderbergh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Soderbergh "Steven Soderbergh")'s action-thriller _[Haywire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haywire\_(2011\_film) "Haywire (2011 film)")_, _[The Vow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Vow\_(2012\_film) "The Vow (2012 film)")_ with [Rachel McAdams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachel_McAdams "Rachel McAdams"), and _[21 Jump Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21\_Jump\_Street\_(film) "21 Jump Street (film)")_ (film adaptation of [TV series of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21_Jump_Street "21 Jump Street")) with [Jonah Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonah_Hill "Jonah Hill").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-24)

Tatum also starred in _[Magic Mike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic\_Mike "Magic Mike")_, a film based on his eight-month experience as a stripper in Florida. The film was directed by Soderbergh,[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-deadline1-25) was co-produced by Tatum and Soderbergh, and starred Tatum as Mike. He is a featured performer at a Tampa, Florida, male strip club who takes a younger dancer ([Alex Pettyfer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Pettyfer "Alex Pettyfer")) under his wing to show him how to hustle "on and off stage".[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-deadline1-25) The film's cast also included [Matt Bomer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Bomer "Matt Bomer"), [Joe Manganiello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello "Joe Manganiello"), and [Matthew McConaughey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_McConaughey "Matthew McConaughey").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-deadline1-25)

## Other ventures

### Business

In October 2012, Tatum and a friend opened the Saints and Sinners burlesque-themed restaurant and bar in New Orleans, which remained open until 2024.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-45)

### Production companies

In an interview with _[Details](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Details\_(magazine) "Details (magazine)")_ magazine, published in early 2012, Tatum said he wants to produce all the films he stars in, "I really don't want to be in any more movies that I don't produce. Unless it's with one of the 10 directors that I really want to work with, I don't have any interest in not being on the ground floor of creating it."[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-46) He, his then-wife [Jenna Dewan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan "Jenna Dewan"), and their production partner [Reid Carolin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reid_Carolin "Reid Carolin") signed a two-year production deal in 2010 with [Relativity Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Relativity_Media "Relativity Media") for any films they may develop during that time.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-47)

Tatum started two production companies, 33andOut Productions[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-48) and Iron Horse Entertainment.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-49) Their first production was the 2010 documentary _[Earth Made of Glass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth\_Made\_of\_Glass\_(film) "Earth Made of Glass (film)")_. In 2021, another one of his production companies, Free Association, signed a first look deal with [MGM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer "Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-50)

### Writing

Tatum has written two picture books inspired by his daughter.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-pmjuneau-51) The first, _The One and Only Sparkella_ (2021), was a #1 [_New York Times_ bestseller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times_Best_Seller_list "The New York Times Best Seller list") for children's picture books the week it published.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-52)_The One and Only Sparkella Makes a Plan_ was published in 2022.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-53)

## Influence

Tatum was named [_People_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_(magazine) "People (magazine)")'s "Sexiest Man Alive" in 2012 and one of _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")_'s [100 most influential people in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_100 "Time 100") in 2022.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-54)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-55)

## Personal life

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fe/Channing_Tatum%2C_Jenna_Dewan_2012.jpg/250px-Channing_Tatum%2C_Jenna_Dewan_2012.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Channing_Tatum,_Jenna_Dewan_2012.jpg)

Tatum and then-wife Jenna Dewan at the [Peabody Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peabody_Awards "Peabody Awards") 2012

In 2006, Tatum met actress [Jenna Dewan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan "Jenna Dewan") on the set of their film _[Step Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Step\_Up\_(film) "Step Up (film)")_, and they married on July 11, 2009, in [Malibu, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malibu,_California "Malibu, California").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-marriage-56) They have one daughter, born in 2013.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-57) On April 2, 2018, the couple announced they were separating.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-58) Six months later, Dewan filed for divorce from Tatum.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-59) The divorce was finalized in November 2019.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-60) In a 2023 interview with _[Vanity Fair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanity\_Fair\_(magazine) "Vanity Fair (magazine)")_, Tatum questioned whether he would ever remarry, though said his divorce prompted self-improvement, including a strong relationship with his daughter.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-pmjuneau-51)

Tatum dated English singer [Jessie J](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessie_J "Jessie J") from 2018 to 2020.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-62)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-63) In 2021, Tatum started dating [Zoë Kravitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zo%C3%AB_Kravitz "Zoë Kravitz") and, by 2023, the couple were [engaged](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engagement "Engagement").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-64)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-65) The engagement was called off in October 2024.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-66) In April 2025, it was confirmed that Tatum is in a relationship with model Inka Williams.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-67)

In February 2026, Tatum suffered a severe shoulder injury that resulted in surgery and him having to drop-out of a film titled _Kockroach._[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-68)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-69)

Tatum is a fan of [anime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anime "Anime"), and has said that he and his daughter, Everly, enjoy watching _[Demon Slayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demon\_Slayer:\_Kimetsu\_no\_Yaiba\_(TV\_series) "Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba (TV series)")_ and _[Black Clover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black\_Clover\_(TV\_series) "Black Clover (TV series)")_.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-70)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-71)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum#cite_note-72)
