**Rebel Melanie Elizabeth Wilson** (born **Melanie Elizabeth Bownds**, 2 March 1980)[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-6) is an Australian actress, comedian and producer. After graduating from the [Australian Theatre for Young People](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Theatre_for_Young_People "Australian Theatre for Young People") in 2003, Wilson began appearing in the [SBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_Broadcasting_Service "Special Broadcasting Service") comedy series _[Pizza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pizza\_(TV\_series) "Pizza (TV series)")_ (2003–2007) and later appeared in the [sketch comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sketch_comedy "Sketch comedy") show _[The Wedge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wedge\_(Australian\_TV\_series) "The Wedge (Australian TV series)")_ (2006–2007). She wrote, produced and starred in the musical comedy series _[Bogan Pride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bogan\_Pride "Bogan Pride")_ (2008). Shortly after moving to the United States, Wilson appeared in the comedy films _[Bridesmaids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridesmaids\_(2011\_film) "Bridesmaids (2011 film)")_ and _[A Few Best Men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Few\_Best\_Men "A Few Best Men")_, both in 2011.

In 2012, Wilson appeared in the comedy films _[What to Expect When You're Expecting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What\_to\_Expect\_When\_You're\_Expecting\_(film) "What to Expect When You're Expecting (film)")_, _[Struck by Lightning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Struck\_by\_Lightning\_(2012\_film) "Struck by Lightning (2012 film)"),_ and _[Bachelorette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelorette\_(film) "Bachelorette (film)")_. Wilson wrote and starred in _[Super Fun Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super\_Fun\_Night "Super Fun Night")_ (2013), a television sitcom that aired for one season on [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company"). She gained wider recognition for her role in the musical comedy _[Pitch Perfect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitch\_Perfect\_(film\_series) "Pitch Perfect (film series)")_[film series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitch_Perfect_(film_series) "Pitch Perfect (film series)") (2012–2017).

In 2019, Wilson had her first lead roles in the comedies [_Isn't It Romantic_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isn't_It_Romantic_(2019_film) "Isn't It Romantic (2019 film)") and [_The Hustle_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hustle_(film) "The Hustle (film)"), and also had a supporting role in the comedy drama _[Jojo Rabbit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jojo\_Rabbit "Jojo Rabbit")_. In 2022, she starred in the [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") comedy film [_Senior Year_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senior_Year_(2022_film) "Senior Year (2022 film)"), also serving as a producer.

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rebel_Wilson&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Rebel Melanie Elizabeth Wilson was born on 2 March 1980[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-ASIC2-2) in [Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney "Sydney"), New South Wales, Australia.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-7) Her parents are [professional dog handlers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_handler "Professional handler"), [dog show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dog_show "Dog show") judges and breeders.[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-11) Wilson grew up in the suburbs of [Kenthurst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenthurst,_New_South_Wales "Kenthurst, New South Wales"), [Parramatta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parramatta "Parramatta") and [Castle Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castle_Hill,_New_South_Wales "Castle Hill, New South Wales").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-12) She attended the independent [Tara Anglican School for Girls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tara_Anglican_School_for_Girls "Tara Anglican School for Girls") as a boarder.[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-16) She completed her [Higher School Certificate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Higher_School_Certificate_(New_South_Wales) "Higher School Certificate (New South Wales)") in 1997, achieving a ranking of 99.3, including second place in the state in Food Technology.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-17)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-:4-18) Wilson joined the debating team and a teacher encouraged her to enter [Tournament of Minds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tournament_of_Minds "Tournament of Minds"), which she credits for helping her come out of her shell. Wilson worked at a cinema in Castle Hill in her younger years, but quit after patrons recognised her after the showing of her first movie, _[Fat Pizza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fat\_Pizza "Fat Pizza")_.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-:4-18)

Wilson is the eldest of four children, with sisters Liberty and Annaleise (who uses the name "Annachi") and a brother, who uses the name "Ryot".[[d]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-22) Liberty and Ryot appeared on the [first season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Amazing_Race_Australia_1 "The Amazing Race Australia 1") of _[The Amazing Race Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Amazing\_Race\_Australia "The Amazing Race Australia")_ in 2011, where they were the first team eliminated.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-23) Wilson has stated that, according to her grandmother, her great-aunt was [Lillian Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lillian_Disney "Lillian Disney"), who was married to [Walt Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney "Walt Disney") until his death in 1966.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-24) Wilson stood by this belief in court, despite there being no evidence to support the claim;[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-Telegraph-25)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-26) it continues to be disputed by genealogist Dale Sheridan.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-27)

Wilson's first career choice was mathematics. She told _[The Sydney Morning Herald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sydney\_Morning\_Herald "The Sydney Morning Herald")_, "I was very academic at high school and was always good with numbers."[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-PushOver-28) She attended the [University of New South Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_New_South_Wales "University of New South Wales"), graduating in 2009 with [Bachelor of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts") (Theatre and Performance Studies) and [Bachelor of Laws](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Laws "Bachelor of Laws") degrees. She planned to be a lawyer, but decided against corporate life and went to the United States to act.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-10things-8)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-29) A former [Rotary International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotary_International "Rotary International") youth ambassador for Australia, she was based in South Africa for one year, where she contracted [malaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaria "Malaria").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-PushOver-28)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-TopTen-30) She has spoken of malaria-induced hallucinations, where she saw herself as an actress who had won an [Oscar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award"), convincing her to pursue an acting career.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-TopTen-30)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rebel_Wilson&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### 2002–2010: early work

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rebel_Wilson&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2002–2010: early work")]

Wilson studied at the [Australian Theatre for Young People](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Theatre_for_Young_People "Australian Theatre for Young People") (ATYP).[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-MeetTheCast-31) In 2003, she moved to [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") after winning the ATYP International scholarship, which was funded by [Nicole Kidman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicole_Kidman "Nicole Kidman"). While in New York, Wilson trained with [The Second City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Second_City "The Second City").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-off_to_New_York-32)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-33) She appeared with the [Sydney Theatre Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney_Theatre_Company "Sydney Theatre Company") and performed at the [Melbourne International Comedy Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne_International_Comedy_Festival "Melbourne International Comedy Festival").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-MeetTheCast-31) She first came to the public's attention in 2002 with her stage musical _The Westie Monologues_, which she wrote,[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-34) starred in and produced in Sydney.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-35) Her follow-up stage productions, which she wrote, produced and starred in include _Spunks_ and _Confessions of an Exchange Student_.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-PushOver-28)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-36)

In Australia, Wilson is also known for her roles as Toula on the [SBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SBS_(Australian_TV_channel) "SBS (Australian TV channel)") comedy series _[Pizza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pizza\_(TV\_series) "Pizza (TV series)")_ and as various characters including Lucy, Fat Mandi and Karla Bangs on the sketch comedy series _[The Wedge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wedge\_(Australian\_TV\_series) "The Wedge (Australian TV series)")_.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-TopTen-30) She played an _[Australian Idol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian\_Idol "Australian Idol")_ mad schoolgirl in a series of [Telstra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telstra "Telstra") advertisements shown during _Australian Idol_ from 2004 to 2005.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-37) She also had roles in the feature films _[Fat Pizza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fat\_Pizza "Fat Pizza")_ (2003) and _[Ghost Rider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghost\_Rider\_(2007\_film) "Ghost Rider (2007 film)")_ (2007).[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-Pride-38)

In 2008, Wilson created, wrote, produced and starred in the musical comedy series _[Bogan Pride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bogan\_Pride "Bogan Pride")_ on SBS One and also starred in the improvisational [Nine Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nine_Network "Nine Network") series _[Monster House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monster\_House\_(Australian\_TV\_series) "Monster House (Australian TV series)")_.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-TopTen-30)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-Pride-38) In 2009 Wilson won the [Tropfest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropfest "Tropfest") Best Actress award for her role in the film _Bargain_.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-AboutTown-39) She has made appearances on the improvisational comedy show _[Thank God You're Here](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thank\_God\_You're\_Here "Thank God You're Here")_ and the comedy game show _[Talkin' 'Bout Your Generation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talkin'\_'Bout\_Your\_Generation "Talkin' 'Bout Your Generation")_.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-MeetTheCast-31)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-40) She performed stand-up on the television special _The Breast Darn Show In Town_ and guest starred in the [Seven Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven_Network "Seven Network") drama _[City Homicide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City\_Homicide "City Homicide")_ and performed improv at the [Upright Citizens Brigade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upright_Citizens_Brigade "Upright Citizens Brigade") in Los Angeles.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-41)

### 2010–present: transition to Hollywood

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rebel_Wilson&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2010–present: transition to Hollywood")]

Not content with her small role in _Ghost Rider_, Wilson moved to the United States in January 2010 and signed to talent and literary agents [William Morris Endeavor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Morris_Endeavor "William Morris Endeavor").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-OurRebel-42) Wilson's next film role came in the [Judd Apatow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judd_Apatow "Judd Apatow") film, _[Bridesmaids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridesmaids\_(2011\_film) "Bridesmaids (2011 film)")_, in which she played Brynn, the sister of [Matt Lucas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Lucas "Matt Lucas")' character.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-OurRebel-42) The role was written especially for her.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-Rafanelli-43) Wilson then appeared in the CBS sitcom _[Rules of Engagement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rules\_of\_Engagement\_(TV\_series) "Rules of Engagement (TV series)")_ and on the [Comedy Central](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_Central "Comedy Central") series, _[Workaholics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workaholics "Workaholics")_.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-Joan-44)

She co-hosted the 2010 [ARIA Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ARIA_Music_Awards "ARIA Music Awards") and performed at the inaugural _Variety_'s Power of Comedy event in Los Angeles with Lucas and [Russell Brand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russell_Brand "Russell Brand").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-Joan-44) In early 2011, Wilson filmed _[A Few Best Men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Few\_Best\_Men "A Few Best Men")_ at Fox Studios Australia.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-45) She also filmed a role in _[Small Apartments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Small\_Apartments "Small Apartments")_.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-Expecting-46) Wilson was named one of _[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety\_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)")_ magazine's "Top Ten Comics to Watch for 2011".[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-TopTen-30) In 2012, Wilson had a role in the ensemble comedy _[What to Expect When You're Expecting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What\_to\_Expect\_When\_You're\_Expecting\_(film) "What to Expect When You're Expecting (film)")_, as Janice,[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-Expecting-46) and co-starred in the indie film _[Struck By Lightning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Struck\_by\_Lightning\_(2012\_film) "Struck by Lightning (2012 film)")_.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-47)

In August 2011, Borys Kit of _[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hollywood\_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")_ reported that Wilson had replaced [Casey Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casey_Wilson "Casey Wilson") in _[Bachelorette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelorette\_(film) "Bachelorette (film)")_.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-Ramps-48) In 2012, Wilson voiced a character in _[Ice Age: Continental Drift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice\_Age:\_Continental\_Drift "Ice Age: Continental Drift")_[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-Ramps-48) and played Fat Amy in _[Pitch Perfect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitch\_Perfect "Pitch Perfect")_. For the latter role, she received critical acclaim and earned various award nominations, including Best Supporting Actress from the [San Diego Film Critics Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Film_Critics_Society "San Diego Film Critics Society") and [Best Actress in a Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/18th_Critics'_Choice_Awards#Best_Actress_in_a_Comedy "18th Critics' Choice Awards") from the [Broadcast Film Critics Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadcast_Film_Critics_Association "Broadcast Film Critics Association").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-SanDiego-49)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-CriticsChoice-50) She won the [MTV Movie Award for Best Actor in a Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Movie_Award_for_Best_Actor_in_a_Movie "MTV Movie Award for Best Actor in a Movie") and shared the Best Musical Moment award with her _Pitch Perfect_ co-stars. Wilson was also nominated for [MTV Movie Award for Best Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Movie_Award_for_Best_Performance "MTV Movie Award for Best Performance").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-Goodacre-51) Wilson later won the Choice Movie Actress: Comedy award for _Pitch Perfect_ at the [2013 Teen Choice Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Teen_Choice_Awards "2013 Teen Choice Awards").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-WSJ-52) She had also been nominated for Choice Comedian at the 2013 Teen Choice Awards.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-Wightman-53)

Wilson in 2019

In January 2012, [Michael Ausiello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Ausiello "Michael Ausiello") of [TVLine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TVLine "TVLine") announced that Wilson would be writing and starring in _[Super Fun Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super\_Fun\_Night "Super Fun Night")_, a comedy that follows three friends on a quest to have fun every Friday night.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-Ausiello-54) The pilot was picked up by [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and [Conan O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_O'Brien "Conan O'Brien") became one of the executive producers.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-Ausiello-54) The pilot was later turned down by CBS, but the [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company") network picked up the project.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-Andreeva-55) A series was ordered and the show began broadcasting in October 2013.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-56) The series was cancelled after one season.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-57) Wilson played Robin Peck in [Michael Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bay "Michael Bay")'s _[Pain & Gain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pain\_&\_Gain "Pain & Gain")_ (2013).[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-58)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-59) She hosted the [2013 MTV Movie Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_MTV_Movie_Awards "2013 MTV Movie Awards") on 14 April 2013.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-60)

In March 2014, the American [satellite television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satellite_television "Satellite television") network [Dish Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dish_Network "Dish Network") launched a marketing campaign for its [Hopper DVR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dish_Hopper_(DVR) "Dish Hopper (DVR)") featuring Wilson as the voice of the eponymous animated kangaroo.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-61) Wilson reprised her role in the sequels _[Pitch Perfect 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitch\_Perfect\_2 "Pitch Perfect 2")_ (2015) and _[Pitch Perfect 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitch\_Perfect\_3 "Pitch Perfect 3")_ (2017).[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-62) She also made a cameo in the television comedy _[Pompidou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pompidou\_(TV\_series) "Pompidou (TV series)")_.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-Rafanelli-43) Wilson joined the voice cast for _[Kung Fu Panda 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kung\_Fu\_Panda\_3 "Kung Fu Panda 3")_;[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-63) however, in September 2015, she was replaced with [Kate Hudson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Hudson "Kate Hudson").[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-64)

Wilson next appeared in the ensemble comedy _[How to Be Single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/How\_to\_Be\_Single "How to Be Single")_, released in February 2016.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-65) Nigel M. Smith of _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_ wrote, "Wilson is the standout, nailing every pratfall she's dealt, but _How to Be Single_ doesn't make strong use of her character."[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-66) Wilson also appeared in the action comedy _[Grimsby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grimsby\_(film) "Grimsby (film)")_.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-67) On 14 February 2016, Wilson presented the nominations for the [Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Actor_in_a_Supporting_Role "BAFTA Award for Best Actor in a Supporting Role") category at the [69th British Academy Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/69th_British_Academy_Film_Awards "69th British Academy Film Awards").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-68) Wilson is one of sixty celebrities who make a cameo in _[Absolutely Fabulous: The Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolutely\_Fabulous:\_The\_Movie "Absolutely Fabulous: The Movie")_.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-69)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rebel_Wilson&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Personal life")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/79/Rebel_Wilson_%286707611099%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Rebel_Wilson_%286707611099%29_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rebel_Wilson_(6707611099)_(cropped).jpg)

Wilson in 2012

In 2013, Wilson created a plus-size T-shirt collection named after her "Fat Mandi" character in _[The Wedge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wedge\_(Australian\_TV\_series) "The Wedge (Australian TV series)")_ featuring images of donuts and cupcakes.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-88) In 2017, Wilson launched a plus-sized clothing range called Rebel Wilson x Angels on the heels of a collaboration with [Torrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torrid_(clothing_retailer) "Torrid (clothing retailer)").[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-89)

Wilson and her _Bridesmaids_ co-star, English actor [Matt Lucas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Lucas "Matt Lucas"), lived together in [West Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Hollywood,_California "West Hollywood, California"),[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-90) from September 2012 until 2015.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-91)

In July 2015, Wilson stated her support for stricter American gun laws following the [2015 Lafayette shooting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Lafayette_shooting "2015 Lafayette shooting"), stating, "I don't like getting political but America you really have to follow Australia's example in gun laws. I don't remember a mass shooting in Australia since they [overhauled the gun laws](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gun_laws_in_Australia#Port_Arthur_massacre_and_its_consequences "Gun laws in Australia"). It seems like every week in America there's a shooting. I just want people to be safe, especially people that are doing one of my favorite things in the world—going out to the movies to have fun."[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-gunlaws-92)[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-gunlaws2-93)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-gunlaws3-94)

In 2014, Wilson paid $3.75 million for her Sydney harbourside home. The 1900s freestanding [Victorian house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victorian_house "Victorian house") underwent $900,000 of renovations. Wilson also settled on a Balmain investment apartment, a conversion of a historic mansion. The New York-inspired terrace home took three years to complete. Wilson paid $1.88 million off the plan in 2015 for the two-bedroom apartment.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-:0-95)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-:1-96)

Wilson is a fan of the [Los Angeles Rams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Rams "Los Angeles Rams") of the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League").[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-97)

As her 40th birthday approached, Wilson made the decision to freeze her eggs, which spurred on her effort to make healthy life changes. She has [polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polycystic_ovarian_syndrome "Polycystic ovarian syndrome"), and suffers from [emotional eating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emotional_eating "Emotional eating") due to pressures of fame.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-98) In November 2022, she announced on Instagram the birth of her first child, a daughter born via surrogacy.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-99)

Wilson publicly [came out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coming_out "Coming out") as being in a same-sex relationship on Instagram in June 2022, revealing her relationship with Ramona Agruma while posting on [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram"), "I thought I was searching for a Disney Prince… but maybe what I really needed all this time was a Disney Princess."[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-100) She chose to announce her relationship with Agruma to pre-empt an article by Andrew Hornery of _[The Sydney Morning Herald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sydney\_Morning\_Herald "The Sydney Morning Herald")_ that would have [outed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outed "Outed") her.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-101)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-102) While _Herald_ editor Bevan Shields initially defended Hornery in the face of widespread backlash, denying they were outing her,[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-103) Hornery later admitted to having made mistakes, and the original article was deleted.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-104) In a tweet on 19 February 2023, Wilson confirmed her engagement to Agruma.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-105) The couple married in Italy on 28 September 2024[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-106) and again in Australia on 29 December 2024.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-107) In December 2025, the couple announced that they are expecting another daughter.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-108) The birth of the couple's second child was announced on Wilson's Instagram account on 4 May 2026.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-Second-1)

### Weight

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rebel_Wilson&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Weight")]

An advocate for [body positivity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_positivity "Body positivity"), Wilson has been a role model for larger women. "There's a lot of pressure on women, especially younger women, to conform to the thin body image," she told the Associated Press. "Not everyone can be that way and no one should be ashamed of how they look or suffer bullying and other forms of abuse because of their size and shape."[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-:2-77)

Throughout her career, Wilson has been known for her plus-sized figure and would often play to it in her acting work with characters such as "Fat Amy," a character in the movie _Pitch Perfect_. In a 2013 interview with _Hunger Magazine_, Wilson stated: "As long as I look like this, I'm going to make fat jokes. All comedians have to use their physicality, so I use my size."[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-109) Wilson said that her agency signed her almost on the spot because they had nobody on their books like her.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-:3-110)

Wilson felt lucky to have her body type and stated that people in the industry would tell her not to lose weight. "For me, I think it's about being comfortable in your own skin. I never want to be too unhealthy, because that's bad. You just want to be comfortable with who you are at whatever size", she said.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-:3-110) In 2016, Wilson said that she felt bigger girls did better in comedy because they are easier to laugh at and used that to her advantage.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-111)

In July 2011, Wilson became a spokesperson for weight loss and nutrition company [Jenny Craig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenny_Craig,_Inc. "Jenny Craig, Inc.") in Australia.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-JC-112)[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-113) In January 2012, Wilson told _[The Daily Telegraph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Daily\_Telegraph\_(Sydney) "The Daily Telegraph (Sydney)")_ that she had lost 10 kilograms (22 lb) since signing up to the program.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-StayingBig-114) In February 2013, she confirmed that she had ended her agreement with Jenny Craig the previous year.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-115)

Wilson asserted that the producers of _[Pitch Perfect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitch\_Perfect "Pitch Perfect")_ had refused to let her lose any more weight during filming, as her contract stated that she must stay the same size. She said that once her film commitments were over, she would start her diet again to reach her target weight of 80 kilograms (180 lb).[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-StayingBig-114)

In her 2020 "year of health", Wilson made it her mission to lose 60 pounds (27 kg) and did so by November 2020. Wilson stated that she has always been confident in how she looked, but now feels "super confident".[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-116)

### Public profile

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rebel_Wilson&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Public profile")]

#### Disputed biography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rebel_Wilson&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Disputed biography")]

In May 2015, Australian magazine _[Woman's Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woman's\_Day\_(Australian\_magazine) "Woman's Day (Australian magazine)")_ published a story claiming that Wilson had been misleading about her birth name, age, and upbringing.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-WomensDay-117) Wilson had previously said in interviews that she was raised by dog-training "[bogan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bogan "Bogan")" parents in the [ghetto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghetto "Ghetto") of Sydney, spent a year in Zimbabwe, climbed into a cage with a leopard, and got caught in a shoot-out and then struck down by a severe strain of [malaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaria "Malaria") from a [mosquito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mosquito "Mosquito") in Mozambique where, from her [intensive care](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intensive_care_unit "Intensive care unit") bed, she envisioned herself winning an [Oscar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") and rapping her acceptance speech.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-118)

Her age was also incorrectly given as 29, when it was actually 35, which she later admitted was something she chose not to correct.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-Telegraph-25)_Woman's Day_ called all of this into question and claimed that Wilson had, on the contrary, a "very normal, upper-middle-class upbringing" and "added a touch of 'fantasy' to the life she led before becoming a household name".[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-WomensDay-117) The story was picked up by several other publications including _The Sydney Morning Herald_, _[People](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People\_(magazine) "People (magazine)")_ magazine,[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-119) the _[Chicago Tribune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_Tribune "Chicago Tribune")_[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-120) and _[The Huffington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HuffPost "HuffPost")_.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-121)

Most notably, Wilson's true birth date was confirmed through business records filed with the [Australian Securities & Investments Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Securities_&_Investments_Commission "Australian Securities & Investments Commission"), which were obtained by _The Sydney Morning Herald_,[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-122) and her birth name of Melanie was confirmed. Following the appeal, Wilson continued to stand by her claim that she is related to Walt Disney by marriage, despite having no evidence to support this.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-123) Following this incident, Wilson was "sacked from two [DreamWorks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DreamWorks_Pictures "DreamWorks Pictures") animations" and "missed out on movie roles during 2015 and 2016".[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-124)

#### Memoir

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rebel_Wilson&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Memoir")]

Wilson's memoir, _Rebel Rising_, was published in April 2024.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-125)[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-126)[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-127)[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-128) It garnered attention for her recounting of discomfort on the set of _[Grimsby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grimsby\_(film) "Grimsby (film)")_, including [Sacha Baron Cohen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacha_Baron_Cohen "Sacha Baron Cohen")'s alleged requests for nudity and inappropriate behavior during a sex scene, which she refused. Baron Cohen has denied these claims through a spokesperson.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-129) Following this episode, publication was pushed back and significant portions of the chapter associated with this incident were redacted for the UK due to legislation regarding factual accuracy and [libel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_defamation_law "English defamation law").[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-130)

#### Lawsuits

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rebel_Wilson&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Lawsuits")]

On 16 May 2016, Wilson said print and online articles in _Woman's Day_, the Australian _Women's Weekly_, _[NW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NW\_(magazine) "NW (magazine)")_ and _OK!_ magazines made her out to be a serial liar. According to a [defamation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defamation "Defamation") writ filed in the [Supreme Court of Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_Victoria "Supreme Court of Victoria"), Wilson said her reputation and credit had suffered and she had been humiliated and embarrassed. She also sued for special damages, claiming she missed out on roles and others were terminated because of the articles.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-131) Wilson was represented by [Matthew Collins QC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_Collins_(barrister) "Matthew Collins (barrister)"). On 15 June 2017, a six-person jury ruled in Wilson's favour, finding that publisher [Bauer Media Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bauer_Media_Group "Bauer Media Group") had indeed wrongly painted the actress as a serial liar, and that publishing the articles was likely to have caused harm to her career.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-132)

On 13 September 2017, Wilson was awarded approximately [A$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_dollar "Australian dollar")4,500,000 in damages; sources conflict on the exact amount. Wilson's lawyer Richard Leder said: "Today's verdict is a significant record—it's about four times the highest previous verdict in a defamation case in Australia." In June 2017, Wilson tweeted: "Any dollars I receive will go to charity, scholarships or invested into the Aussie film industry to provide jobs."[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-133)[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-134)

Bauer Media appealed the amount of the damages.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-135) On 14 June 2018, Bauer Media won its appeal; the damages were reduced to $600,000, and Wilson was ordered to repay more than A$4,000,000 of the initial settlement. She also had to cover 80% of what Bauer spent on its appeal.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-136)[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-137) Wilson announced her intention to appeal against the decision,[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-138) and lodged an appeal with the High Court on 11 July 2018.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-139) The High Court refused the application on 16 November 2018.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-140)[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-141)

Main article: [The Deb (film) §Legal dispute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Deb_(film)#Legal_dispute "The Deb (film)")

Wilson was subject to a defamation suit at the [Federal Court of Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Court_of_Australia "Federal Court of Australia") in Sydney in April 2026, lodged by Charlotte MacInnes, an actor who appeared in Wilson's film _[The Deb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Deb\_(film) "The Deb (film)")_. In Instagram posts in 2024 and 2025, Wilson alleged that the actor had accused a producer of harassment but then withdrawn the accusation in exchange for career benefits.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-142)[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-143) The case was dismissed with Australia Federal Court Justice Elisabeth Raper ordering that Wilson's costs be repaid by MacInnes.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-144)[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebel_Wilson#cite_note-145)
