_**The Girl Next Door**_ is a 2004 American [romantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romantic_comedy "Romantic comedy")[sex comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_comedy "Sexual comedy") film directed by [Luke Greenfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luke_Greenfield "Luke Greenfield") and written by David Wagner, Brent Goldberg, and [Stuart Blumberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stuart_Blumberg "Stuart Blumberg"), and starring Emile Hirsch, [Elisha Cuthbert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elisha_Cuthbert "Elisha Cuthbert"), [Timothy Olyphant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timothy_Olyphant "Timothy Olyphant"), [James Remar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Remar "James Remar"), [Chris Marquette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Marquette "Chris Marquette"), and [Paul Dano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Dano "Paul Dano"). The story follows Matthew Kidman, a [high school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secondary_school "Secondary school") senior who falls in love with his new neighbor, Danielle, and discovers she is a former [adult film actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pornographic_film_actor "Pornographic film actor"). It marked [Olivia Wilde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olivia_Wilde "Olivia Wilde")'s film debut.

Development for _The Girl Next Door_ began as early as 2001. The film's screenplay was partly inspired by _[Risky Business](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Risky\_Business "Risky Business")_ (1983).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-GNDCastVar-10) Principal photography occurred primarily in [Los Angeles County, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_County,_California "Los Angeles County, California") and [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas "Las Vegas"). The film features cinematography by Eric Alan Edwards and a score by [Paul Haslinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Haslinger "Paul Haslinger").

_The Girl Next Door_ premiered at the Texas Film Festival on February 18, 2004, before being theatrically distributed nationwide by [20th Century Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20th_Century_Studios "20th Century Studios") on April 9, 2004. It received mixed reviews, with critics praising for its performances, but criticism for tonal inconsistencies, and [underperformed at the box office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Box-office_bomb "Box-office bomb"). However, _The Girl Next Door_ later gained a [cult following](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cult_following "Cult following") through home media and television, with retrospective appreciation for its genre subversion and portrayal of the adult entertainment industry.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-Rosen-2)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-Carp-11)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-Sneider-12)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-McDermott-13)

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

Matthew Kidman, an ambitious [high school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secondary_school "Secondary school") senior in suburban [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California"), has been accepted to [Georgetown University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgetown_University "Georgetown University") but lacks the funds to attend. As [class president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Class_president "Class president"), he raises $25,000 to help a Cambodian student, Samnang Sok, study in the United States, but feels his own high school experience has been uneventful. His closest friends, Eli Brooks and Tim Klitz, are more focused on mischief and [adult films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pornographic_film "Pornographic film") than academics or self-reflection.

Matthew's routine changes when Danielle Clark, an attractive young woman, moves in next door. After a series of playful and flirtatious interactions, the two begin a tentative romance. Their relationship is disrupted when Matthew learns from Eli that Danielle is a former [adult film actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pornographic_film_actor "Pornographic film actor"). Following misguided advice from his friend, Matthew takes Danielle to a [motel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motel "Motel") and treats her inappropriately, leading her to end the relationship and consider returning to the [adult industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_industry "Sex industry").

Determined to make amends, Matthew tracks Danielle to an adult film convention in [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas "Las Vegas"), where he confronts her former [producer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_producer "Film producer") and ex-boyfriend, Kelly. Despite Kelly's threats, Matthew convinces Danielle to leave the industry. Days later, Kelly retaliates by abducting Matthew and coercing him into stealing from a rival producer, Hugo Posh. After narrowly escaping police capture, Matthew arrives at a [scholarship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scholarship "Scholarship") dinner under the influence of [ecstasy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MDMA "MDMA") and gives an impromptu speech but fails to secure the award.

Kelly escalates the conflict by posing as a school advisor and stealing the $25,000 fund. To recover the money and clear Matthew's name, Danielle proposes producing an adult film featuring her former colleagues and Matthew's classmates during their senior [prom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prom "Prom"). Eli directs the film, and Klitz unexpectedly steps into a key role. The project is a success, and Matthew and Danielle have sex.

The next day, Kelly arrives at Matthew's home with a copy of the film, threatening to expose him and ruin his chances of attending Georgetown. However, upon viewing it, Matthew's parents and principal are surprised to find that it is a modern [sex education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_education "Sex education") video. Realizing the film's value, they reluctantly support its distribution. Kelly, impressed by Matthew's cleverness, begrudgingly concedes defeat.

Matthew partners with Hugo Posh to distribute the film, earning more than enough to fund Samnang's education and pay for his tuition. He also sends Kelly a box of [cigars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cigar "Cigar"), thereby burying the hatchet between them. Eli begins a promising film career immediately after High School, Klitz gains new confidence from his role in the adult film, and Matthew departs for Georgetown with Danielle by his side.

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Production")]

### Development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Development")]

In May 2001, it was reported that [Luke Greenfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luke_Greenfield "Luke Greenfield") was developing the [teen comedy film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen_film "Teen film")_The Girl Next Door_, which Greenfield co-scripted with [Chris McKenna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_McKenna_(writer) "Chris McKenna (writer)"), at [20th Century Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20th_Century_Studios "20th Century Studios")-based production company [Regency Enterprises](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regency_Enterprises "Regency Enterprises").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-RegencyGNDVar-14) Greenfield had held on to the script for over a year hoping to make a film in the vein of _[Risky Business](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Risky\_Business "Risky Business")_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-RegencyGNDVar-14)

Commenting on the film's original screenplay, Greenfield said: "It was a different film. It was very tawdry, a teen sex comedy. It was just nothing like what I wanted to do. But the premise, of a kid falling in love with a porn star who moves in next door and is trying to escape her past, really excited me on a number of levels."[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-Rosen-2) The screenplay was reworked with contributions from [Stuart Blumberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stuart_Blumberg "Stuart Blumberg").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-Rosen-2) While Greenfield and McKenna contributed to the film's story and screenplay, neither were credited; Blumberg, David T. Wagner, and Brent Goldberg received screenwriting credit.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-Rosen-2) Greenfield noted: "I directed the movie, so at least I got credit, but Chris really got screwed. He really did. He never got his name on it."[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-Rosen-2)

### Casting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Casting")]

Greenfield [auditioned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audition "Audition") a number of actors for the film, including [Katherine Heigl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katherine_Heigl "Katherine Heigl") and [Chris Evans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Evans_(actor) "Chris Evans (actor)").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-Rosen-2) In October 2002, it was reported that Emile Hirsch and [Elisha Cuthbert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elisha_Cuthbert "Elisha Cuthbert") had signed on to star in the film as Matthew and Danielle, respectively.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-GNDCastVar-10) Hirsch was cast after Greenfield saw an audition tape he had recorded for [Gus Van Sant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gus_Van_Sant "Gus Van Sant")'s _[Elephant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elephant\_(2003\_film) "Elephant (2003 film)")_ (2003).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-Rosen-2) For the role of Danielle, the studio originally sought [Katie Holmes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katie_Holmes "Katie Holmes"), but Greenfield insisted on casting Cuthbert, who had recently completed _[Old School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old\_School\_(2003\_film) "Old School (2003 film)")_ (2003).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-Rosen-2) "She was so hungry. I remember meeting her and she had done so much preparation," Greenfield recalled. "She had all these pictures of different looks that Danielle would have. She was 20 years old at the time. She was talking about the character and she had such maturity".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-Rosen-2)

[Timothy Olyphant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timothy_Olyphant "Timothy Olyphant") was cast in the role of Danielle's ex-boyfriend and manager, Kelly, after [Brad Pitt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt "Brad Pitt") passed on the project.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-Rosen-2)[Olivia Wilde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olivia_Wilde "Olivia Wilde"), who had originally worked as a casting intern on the project, made her screen debut in the film in a minor role as high school student Kellie.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-Rosen-2)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-eonline/1396740-15)

### Filming

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Filming")]

_The Girl Next Door_ was shot in Southern California,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-thennowmovie/girl-next-door-16) including in [Long Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_Beach,_California "Long Beach, California"),[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-thennowmovie/girl-next-door-16)[Glendale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glendale,_California "Glendale, California"),[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-movie-locations/TGND-17) and [Pasadena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pasadena,_California "Pasadena, California"). Some filming was completed at the [Huntington Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntington_Library "Huntington Library") and [Doheny Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doheny_Library "Doheny Library") at the [University of Southern California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Southern_California "University of Southern California").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-thecinemaholic/TGND-18)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-19) Additional photography occurred on the [Paramount Ranch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount_Ranch "Paramount Ranch").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-20) Principal photography began in January 2003.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-21)

## Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Release")]

_The Girl Next Door_ premiered at the Texas Film Festival at [Texas A&M University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_A&M_University "Texas A&M University") on February 18, 2004,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-24) followed by [sneak previews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sneak_preview "Sneak preview") in select cities on March 20, 2004.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-25) It was subsequently theatrically released in the United States by [20th Century Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20th_Century_Studios "20th Century Studios") on April 9, 2004, opening in 2,148 theaters.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-AFI-4)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-BOM-9)

### Home video and rights

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Home video and rights")]

On August 24, 2004, [20th Century Fox Home Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20th_Century_Fox_Home_Entertainment "20th Century Fox Home Entertainment") released an unrated version of the film on DVD.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-26) 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment also released this unrated version on [Blu-ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blu-ray "Blu-ray") on September 1, 2009.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-27)

In 2019, [Rupert Murdoch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rupert_Murdoch "Rupert Murdoch") sold most of [21st Century Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21st_Century_Fox "21st Century Fox")'s film and television assets to [Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walt_Disney_Company "The Walt Disney Company"). However, much of _The Girl Next Door'_ s underlying rights were with production company [Regency Enterprises](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regency_Enterprises "Regency Enterprises") rather than Fox, and Twentieth Century Fox Film Corporation are not mentioned as one of the copyright holders in the credits.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-28) At the time of the sale, Fox had a 20% stake in Regency Enterprises, and this 20% stake was transferred to Disney when they purchased the Fox entertainment assets.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-29)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Reception")]

### Box office

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Box office")]

_The Girl Next Door_ grossed $14.6 million in the United States and Canada, and $15.8 million in international markets, for a worldwide total of approximately $30.4 million.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-BOM-9)

### Critical response

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Critical response")]

On the [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator")[Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), the film holds an approval rating of 56% based on 159 reviews, with an average score of 5.6/10. The website's consensus reads, "The movie borrows heavily from _[Risky Business](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Risky\_Business "Risky Business")_ (1983), though Emile Hirsch and [Elisha Cuthbert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elisha_Cuthbert "Elisha Cuthbert") are appealing leads."[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-30)[Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic") reports a weighted average score of 47 out of 100, based on 32 critics, indicating "mixed or average reviews."[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-31) Audiences polled by [CinemaScore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CinemaScore "CinemaScore") gave the film an average grade of "B+" on an A+ to F scale.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-32)

Sheri Linden of _[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hollywood\_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")_ praised the film as a "sharp, vivacious comedy."[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-33)[Desson Thomson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desson_Thomson "Desson Thomson") of _[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Washington\_Post "The Washington Post")_ described it as "an entertaining affair whose wild-card creativity never ceases to surprise."[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-34) Writing for _[Entertainment Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment\_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")_, [Owen Gleiberman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Owen_Gleiberman "Owen Gleiberman") gave the film a "B−", noting that while it was derivative, "this genial cardboard knockoff is contrived from the start but gets better as it goes along."[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-35)

In a more mixed review, [Joe Leydon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Leydon "Joe Leydon") of [_Variety_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)") criticized the film's "shamelessly derivative" script, drawing comparisons to _Risky Business_, _[American Pie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Pie\_(film) "American Pie (film)")_ (1999), and 1980s teen romances. He described the lead performances as "attractive but bland," though he praised [Timothy Olyphant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timothy_Olyphant "Timothy Olyphant")'s "scene-stealing turn."[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-Leydon-36)[A. O. Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A._O._Scott "A. O. Scott") of _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ observed that the film presents a "nonjudgmental, even celebratory" view of pornography but noted a contradictory tone in portraying Danielle as someone in need of rescue. He concluded that the film "wallow[s]" in its own contradiction without offering much genuine pleasure.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-37)[Roger Ebert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Ebert "Roger Ebert") of the _[Chicago Sun-Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_Sun-Times "Chicago Sun-Times")_ gave the film one and a half stars out of four, calling it a "nasty piece of business" and criticizing its misleading marketing as a teen comedy.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-38)

_**The Girl Next Door**_ is a 2004 American [romantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romantic_comedy "Romantic comedy")[sex comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_comedy "Sexual comedy") film directed by [Luke Greenfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luke_Greenfield "Luke Greenfield") and written by David Wagner, Brent Goldberg, and [Stuart Blumberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stuart_Blumberg "Stuart Blumberg"), and starring Emile Hirsch, [Elisha Cuthbert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elisha_Cuthbert "Elisha Cuthbert"), [Timothy Olyphant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timothy_Olyphant "Timothy Olyphant"), [James Remar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Remar "James Remar"), [Chris Marquette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Marquette "Chris Marquette"), and [Paul Dano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Dano "Paul Dano"). The story follows Matthew Kidman, a [high school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secondary_school "Secondary school") senior who falls in love with his new neighbor, Danielle, and discovers she is a former [adult film actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pornographic_film_actor "Pornographic film actor"). It marked [Olivia Wilde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olivia_Wilde "Olivia Wilde")'s film debut.

Development for _The Girl Next Door_ began as early as 2001. The film's screenplay was partly inspired by _[Risky Business](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Risky\_Business "Risky Business")_ (1983).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-GNDCastVar-10) Principal photography occurred primarily in [Los Angeles County, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_County,_California "Los Angeles County, California") and [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas "Las Vegas"). The film features cinematography by Eric Alan Edwards and a score by [Paul Haslinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Haslinger "Paul Haslinger").

_The Girl Next Door_ premiered at the Texas Film Festival on February 18, 2004, before being theatrically distributed nationwide by [20th Century Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20th_Century_Studios "20th Century Studios") on April 9, 2004. It received mixed reviews, with critics praising for its performances, but criticism for tonal inconsistencies, and [underperformed at the box office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Box-office_bomb "Box-office bomb"). However, _The Girl Next Door_ later gained a [cult following](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cult_following "Cult following") through home media and television, with retrospective appreciation for its genre subversion and portrayal of the adult entertainment industry.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-Rosen-2)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-Carp-11)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-Sneider-12)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-McDermott-13)

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

Matthew Kidman, an ambitious [high school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secondary_school "Secondary school") senior in suburban [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California"), has been accepted to [Georgetown University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgetown_University "Georgetown University") but lacks the funds to attend. As [class president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Class_president "Class president"), he raises $25,000 to help a Cambodian student, Samnang Sok, study in the United States, but feels his own high school experience has been uneventful. His closest friends, Eli Brooks and Tim Klitz, are more focused on mischief and [adult films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pornographic_film "Pornographic film") than academics or self-reflection.

Matthew's routine changes when Danielle Clark, an attractive young woman, moves in next door. After a series of playful and flirtatious interactions, the two begin a tentative romance. Their relationship is disrupted when Matthew learns from Eli that Danielle is a former [adult film actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pornographic_film_actor "Pornographic film actor"). Following misguided advice from his friend, Matthew takes Danielle to a [motel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motel "Motel") and treats her inappropriately, leading her to end the relationship and consider returning to the [adult industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_industry "Sex industry").

Determined to make amends, Matthew tracks Danielle to an adult film convention in [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas "Las Vegas"), where he confronts her former [producer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_producer "Film producer") and ex-boyfriend, Kelly. Despite Kelly's threats, Matthew convinces Danielle to leave the industry. Days later, Kelly retaliates by abducting Matthew and coercing him into stealing from a rival producer, Hugo Posh. After narrowly escaping police capture, Matthew arrives at a [scholarship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scholarship "Scholarship") dinner under the influence of [ecstasy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MDMA "MDMA") and gives an impromptu speech but fails to secure the award.

Kelly escalates the conflict by posing as a school advisor and stealing the $25,000 fund. To recover the money and clear Matthew's name, Danielle proposes producing an adult film featuring her former colleagues and Matthew's classmates during their senior [prom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prom "Prom"). Eli directs the film, and Klitz unexpectedly steps into a key role. The project is a success, and Matthew and Danielle have sex.

The next day, Kelly arrives at Matthew's home with a copy of the film, threatening to expose him and ruin his chances of attending Georgetown. However, upon viewing it, Matthew's parents and principal are surprised to find that it is a modern [sex education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_education "Sex education") video. Realizing the film's value, they reluctantly support its distribution. Kelly, impressed by Matthew's cleverness, begrudgingly concedes defeat.

Matthew partners with Hugo Posh to distribute the film, earning more than enough to fund Samnang's education and pay for his tuition. He also sends Kelly a box of [cigars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cigar "Cigar"), thereby burying the hatchet between them. Eli begins a promising film career immediately after High School, Klitz gains new confidence from his role in the adult film, and Matthew departs for Georgetown with Danielle by his side.

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Production")]

### Development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Development")]

In May 2001, it was reported that [Luke Greenfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luke_Greenfield "Luke Greenfield") was developing the [teen comedy film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen_film "Teen film")_The Girl Next Door_, which Greenfield co-scripted with [Chris McKenna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_McKenna_(writer) "Chris McKenna (writer)"), at [20th Century Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20th_Century_Studios "20th Century Studios")-based production company [Regency Enterprises](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regency_Enterprises "Regency Enterprises").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-RegencyGNDVar-14) Greenfield had held on to the script for over a year hoping to make a film in the vein of _[Risky Business](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Risky\_Business "Risky Business")_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-RegencyGNDVar-14)

Commenting on the film's original screenplay, Greenfield said: "It was a different film. It was very tawdry, a teen sex comedy. It was just nothing like what I wanted to do. But the premise, of a kid falling in love with a porn star who moves in next door and is trying to escape her past, really excited me on a number of levels."[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-Rosen-2) The screenplay was reworked with contributions from [Stuart Blumberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stuart_Blumberg "Stuart Blumberg").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-Rosen-2) While Greenfield and McKenna contributed to the film's story and screenplay, neither were credited; Blumberg, David T. Wagner, and Brent Goldberg received screenwriting credit.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-Rosen-2) Greenfield noted: "I directed the movie, so at least I got credit, but Chris really got screwed. He really did. He never got his name on it."[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-Rosen-2)

### Casting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Casting")]

Greenfield [auditioned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audition "Audition") a number of actors for the film, including [Katherine Heigl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katherine_Heigl "Katherine Heigl") and [Chris Evans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Evans_(actor) "Chris Evans (actor)").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-Rosen-2) In October 2002, it was reported that Emile Hirsch and [Elisha Cuthbert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elisha_Cuthbert "Elisha Cuthbert") had signed on to star in the film as Matthew and Danielle, respectively.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-GNDCastVar-10) Hirsch was cast after Greenfield saw an audition tape he had recorded for [Gus Van Sant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gus_Van_Sant "Gus Van Sant")'s _[Elephant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elephant\_(2003\_film) "Elephant (2003 film)")_ (2003).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-Rosen-2) For the role of Danielle, the studio originally sought [Katie Holmes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katie_Holmes "Katie Holmes"), but Greenfield insisted on casting Cuthbert, who had recently completed _[Old School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old\_School\_(2003\_film) "Old School (2003 film)")_ (2003).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-Rosen-2) "She was so hungry. I remember meeting her and she had done so much preparation," Greenfield recalled. "She had all these pictures of different looks that Danielle would have. She was 20 years old at the time. She was talking about the character and she had such maturity".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-Rosen-2)

[Timothy Olyphant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timothy_Olyphant "Timothy Olyphant") was cast in the role of Danielle's ex-boyfriend and manager, Kelly, after [Brad Pitt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt "Brad Pitt") passed on the project.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-Rosen-2)[Olivia Wilde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olivia_Wilde "Olivia Wilde"), who had originally worked as a casting intern on the project, made her screen debut in the film in a minor role as high school student Kellie.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-Rosen-2)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-eonline/1396740-15)

### Filming

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Filming")]

_The Girl Next Door_ was shot in Southern California,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-thennowmovie/girl-next-door-16) including in [Long Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_Beach,_California "Long Beach, California"),[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-thennowmovie/girl-next-door-16)[Glendale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glendale,_California "Glendale, California"),[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-movie-locations/TGND-17) and [Pasadena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pasadena,_California "Pasadena, California"). Some filming was completed at the [Huntington Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntington_Library "Huntington Library") and [Doheny Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doheny_Library "Doheny Library") at the [University of Southern California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Southern_California "University of Southern California").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-thecinemaholic/TGND-18)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-19) Additional photography occurred on the [Paramount Ranch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount_Ranch "Paramount Ranch").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-20) Principal photography began in January 2003.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-21)

## Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Release")]

_The Girl Next Door_ premiered at the Texas Film Festival at [Texas A&M University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_A&M_University "Texas A&M University") on February 18, 2004,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-24) followed by [sneak previews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sneak_preview "Sneak preview") in select cities on March 20, 2004.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-25) It was subsequently theatrically released in the United States by [20th Century Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20th_Century_Studios "20th Century Studios") on April 9, 2004, opening in 2,148 theaters.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-AFI-4)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-BOM-9)

### Home video and rights

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Home video and rights")]

On August 24, 2004, [20th Century Fox Home Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20th_Century_Fox_Home_Entertainment "20th Century Fox Home Entertainment") released an unrated version of the film on DVD.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-26) 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment also released this unrated version on [Blu-ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blu-ray "Blu-ray") on September 1, 2009.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-27)

In 2019, [Rupert Murdoch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rupert_Murdoch "Rupert Murdoch") sold most of [21st Century Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21st_Century_Fox "21st Century Fox")'s film and television assets to [Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walt_Disney_Company "The Walt Disney Company"). However, much of _The Girl Next Door'_ s underlying rights were with production company [Regency Enterprises](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regency_Enterprises "Regency Enterprises") rather than Fox, and Twentieth Century Fox Film Corporation are not mentioned as one of the copyright holders in the credits.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-28) At the time of the sale, Fox had a 20% stake in Regency Enterprises, and this 20% stake was transferred to Disney when they purchased the Fox entertainment assets.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-29)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Reception")]

### Box office

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Box office")]

_The Girl Next Door_ grossed $14.6 million in the United States and Canada, and $15.8 million in international markets, for a worldwide total of approximately $30.4 million.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-BOM-9)

### Critical response

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Critical response")]

On the [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator")[Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), the film holds an approval rating of 56% based on 159 reviews, with an average score of 5.6/10. The website's consensus reads, "The movie borrows heavily from _[Risky Business](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Risky\_Business "Risky Business")_ (1983), though Emile Hirsch and [Elisha Cuthbert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elisha_Cuthbert "Elisha Cuthbert") are appealing leads."[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-30)[Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic") reports a weighted average score of 47 out of 100, based on 32 critics, indicating "mixed or average reviews."[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-31) Audiences polled by [CinemaScore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CinemaScore "CinemaScore") gave the film an average grade of "B+" on an A+ to F scale.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-32)

Sheri Linden of _[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hollywood\_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")_ praised the film as a "sharp, vivacious comedy."[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-33)[Desson Thomson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desson_Thomson "Desson Thomson") of _[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Washington\_Post "The Washington Post")_ described it as "an entertaining affair whose wild-card creativity never ceases to surprise."[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-34) Writing for _[Entertainment Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment\_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")_, [Owen Gleiberman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Owen_Gleiberman "Owen Gleiberman") gave the film a "B−", noting that while it was derivative, "this genial cardboard knockoff is contrived from the start but gets better as it goes along."[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-35)

In a more mixed review, [Joe Leydon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Leydon "Joe Leydon") of [_Variety_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)") criticized the film's "shamelessly derivative" script, drawing comparisons to _Risky Business_, _[American Pie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Pie\_(film) "American Pie (film)")_ (1999), and 1980s teen romances. He described the lead performances as "attractive but bland," though he praised [Timothy Olyphant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timothy_Olyphant "Timothy Olyphant")'s "scene-stealing turn."[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-Leydon-36)[A. O. Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A._O._Scott "A. O. Scott") of _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ observed that the film presents a "nonjudgmental, even celebratory" view of pornography but noted a contradictory tone in portraying Danielle as someone in need of rescue. He concluded that the film "wallow[s]" in its own contradiction without offering much genuine pleasure.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-37)[Roger Ebert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Ebert "Roger Ebert") of the _[Chicago Sun-Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_Sun-Times "Chicago Sun-Times")_ gave the film one and a half stars out of four, calling it a "nasty piece of business" and criticizing its misleading marketing as a teen comedy.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Next_Door_(2004_film)#cite_note-38)
